title.zh: 卷250 列傳三十七 李霨 孙廷铨 杜立德 冯溥 王熙 吴正治 黄机 宋德宜 伊桑阿 阿兰泰 徐元文
title.en: Volume 250 Biographies 37: Li Wei, Sun Tingquan, Du Lide, Feng Pu, Wang Xi, Wu Zhengzhi, Huang Ji, Song Deyi, Yi Sanga, A Lan Tai, Xu Yuanwen
title.raw: 卷250 列傳三十七 李霨 孙廷铨 杜立德 冯溥 王熙 吴正治 黄机 宋德宜 伊桑阿 阿兰泰 徐元文

sentences.zh: 李霨，字坦園，直隸高陽人，明大學士國𣚴子。

translations.literal: Li Wei, style name Tanyuan, a native of Gaoyang in Zhili, son of Li Guochong, Grand Secretary of the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Li Wei, courtesy name Tanyuan, was a native of Gaoyang in Zhili and the son of Li Guochong, who had served as Grand Secretary under the Ming.

sentences.zh: 少孤，劬學自厲。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he studied laboriously and urged himself on.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in youth, he applied himself to study with tireless discipline.

sentences.zh: 順治三年，成進士，選庶吉士，授檢討，進編修。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shunzhi he became a jinshi, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, appointed reviser, and advanced to compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Shunzhi he passed the jinshi examination, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, was appointed reviser, and was later promoted to compiler.

sentences.zh: 十年，世祖親試習國書翰林，霨列上等，擢中允。

translations.literal: In the tenth year the Shizu Emperor personally tested Hanlin scholars studying the national script; Li Wei was ranked in the upper class and was promoted to junior vice president of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year the Shunzhi Emperor personally examined Hanlin scholars in Manchu; Li Wei ranked in the top class and was promoted to junior vice president of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 累遷秘書院學士。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Bachelor of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive promotions to Bachelor of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時初設日講官，霨與學士麻勒吉、胡兆龍，侍讀學士折庫納，洗馬王熙，中允方懸成、曹本榮等併入直。

translations.literal: At that time the daily lecture office was first established; Li Wei, together with Bachelors Maleqi and Hu Zhaolong, Associate Reader Zhekuna, Court of Imperial Stud Reader Wang Xi, and Junior Vice Presidents Fang Xuancheng and Cao Benrong, among others, all entered regular attendance at court.
translations.idiomatic: When the office of daily lecturers was first established, Li Wei joined Bachelors Maleqi and Hu Zhaolong, Associate Reader Zhekuna, Reader of the Court of Imperial Stud Wang Xi, and Junior Vice Presidents Fang Xuancheng and Cao Benrong, among others, in regular attendance at court.

sentences.zh: 尋充經筵講官。

translations.literal: Soon he also served as a lecture official at the classics lecture.
translations.idiomatic: He soon became a lecturer at the imperial classics lecture.

sentences.zh: 十五年，拜秘書院大學士。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 內三院改內閣，以霨為東閣大學士，兼工部尚書，加太子太保。

translations.literal: When the Three Inner Courts were reorganized as the Grand Secretariat, Li Wei was made Grand Secretary of the Eastern Lodge, concurrently Minister of Works, and granted the title Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When the Three Inner Courts were reorganized as the Grand Secretariat, he was made Grand Secretary of the Eastern Lodge, concurrently served as Minister of Works, and was granted the title Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 以票擬疏誤，鐫四秩。

translations.literal: For errors in drafting memorial responses, he was demoted four ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Because of mistakes in drafting memorial responses, he was demoted four ranks in salary grade.

sentences.zh: 未幾，复官，任事如故。

translations.literal: Before long his office was restored and he served as before.
translations.idiomatic: Before long his post was restored, and he carried on his duties as before.

sentences.zh: 偕大學士巴哈納等校定律例。

translations.literal: Together with Grand Secretary Bahana and others, he collated and revised the legal code.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Grand Secretary Bahana and others, he collated and revised the legal code.

sentences.zh: 十八年，聖祖即位，复內三院，以霨為弘文院大學士。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, when the Kangxi Emperor assumed the throne, the Three Inner Courts were restored and Li Wei was made Grand Secretary of the Hongwen Court.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year, when the Kangxi Emperor ascended the throne, the Three Inner Courts were restored and Li Wei was appointed Grand Secretary of the Hongwen Court.

sentences.zh: 時四大臣輔政，決機務，或議事齟齬，霨輒默然，既乃出片言定是非，票擬或未當，不輕論執。

translations.literal: At that time four great ministers assisted in government and decided affairs of state; when deliberations clashed, Li Wei would remain silent, then offer a brief remark that settled right and wrong; if a draft response was inappropriate, he did not lightly insist on his view.
translations.idiomatic: At that time four senior ministers governed as regents and decided state affairs; when their deliberations deadlocked, Li Wei would hold his tongue, then offer a few words that settled the matter; if a draft memorial response was off the mark, he did not lightly press his own view.

sentences.zh: 每於談笑間婉言曲喻，徐使更正。

translations.literal: Often amid conversation he would gently persuade with indirect words and gradually lead them to correct their views.
translations.idiomatic: Often in the course of conversation he would gently persuade by indirection and gradually bring others to correct their views.

sentences.zh: 其間調和匡救，保護善類，霨有力焉。

translations.literal: In mediating disputes, remedying errors, and protecting worthy men, Li Wei played an important part.
translations.idiomatic: In reconciling differences, remedying wrongs, and protecting worthy men, Li Wei exerted considerable influence.

sentences.zh: 康熙八年夏，旱，奉詔清刑獄，釋系囚，多所平反。

translations.literal: In the summer of the eighth year of Kangxi, during drought, by imperial order he cleared the penal prisons, released prisoners held in custody, and overturned many wrongful convictions.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the eighth year of Kangxi, during a drought, by imperial order he reviewed the penal prisons, released prisoners held in custody, and overturned many wrongful convictions.

sentences.zh: 明年，复內閣，霨以保和殿大學士兼戶部尚書。

translations.literal: The next year the Grand Secretariat was restored, and Li Wei served as Grand Secretary of the Hall of Preserving Harmony, concurrently Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the Grand Secretariat was restored, and Li Wei served as Grand Secretary of the Hall of Preserving Harmony while also holding the post of Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 與修世祖實錄，充總裁官。

translations.literal: He took part in compiling the Veritable Records of the Shizu Emperor and served as chief compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in compiling the Veritable Records of the Shunzhi Emperor and served as chief compiler.

sentences.zh: 十一年，書成，賜銀幣、鞍馬，晉太子太傅。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, when the work was completed, he was granted silver coins and saddle horses and promoted to Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, when the work was completed, he was granted silver coins and saddle horses and was promoted to Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 未幾，三籓叛，繼以察哈爾部作亂。

translations.literal: Before long the Three Feudatories rebelled, followed by unrest in the Chahar tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Three Feudatories rose in rebellion, followed by unrest among the Chahar tribes.

sentences.zh: 上命將出征，凡機密詔旨，每口授霨起草，退直嘗至夜分，或留宿閣中。

translations.literal: When the emperor ordered the generals to campaign, for every confidential edict he would dictate orally to Li Wei to draft; after leaving court Li Wei often worked until midnight, or stayed overnight in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor ordered the army to take the field, every confidential edict was dictated orally for Li Wei to draft; after leaving court he often worked until midnight, or stayed overnight in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 所治職務，出未嘗告人，忠謹慎密，始終匪懈。

translations.literal: The duties he handled, once completed, he never spoke of to others; he was loyal, cautious, and secret, and from beginning to end never slackened.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever business he handled, once done he never spoke of it to others; he was loyal, cautious, and discreet, and from first to last never slackened.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，重修太宗實錄成，進太子太師。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, when the revised Veritable Records of Taizong were completed, he was promoted to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year, when the revised Veritable Records of Taizong were completed, he was promoted to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 台灣初定，提督施琅請設官鎮守，廷議未決。

translations.literal: When Taiwan had just been pacified, Admiral Shi Lang requested that officials be stationed to garrison it, but the court deliberation had not reached a decision.
translations.idiomatic: When Taiwan had just been pacified, Admiral Shi Lang asked that officials be posted to garrison the island, but the court had not yet reached a decision.

sentences.zh: 有謂宜遷其人、棄其地者，上問閣臣，霨言：「台灣孤懸海外，屏蔽閩疆。

translations.literal: Some said the populace should be relocated and the territory abandoned. The emperor asked the grand secretaries; Li Wei said: "Taiwan stands isolated beyond the sea and shields the coast of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Some argued that the people should be relocated and the territory abandoned. The emperor asked the grand secretaries; Li Wei said: "Taiwan stands alone beyond the sea and shields the coast of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 棄其地，恐為外國所據；

translations.literal: If we abandon the territory, I fear it will be seized by a foreign power;
translations.idiomatic: If we abandon the territory, I fear a foreign power will seize it;

sentences.zh: 遷其人，慮有姦宄生事。

translations.literal: if we relocate the people, I fear malcontents will stir up trouble.
translations.idiomatic: if we relocate the people, I fear malcontents will stir up trouble.

sentences.zh: 應如瑯議。」

translations.literal: We should follow Lang's proposal."
translations.idiomatic: We should follow Lang's proposal."

sentences.zh: 上韙之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，卒，諡文勤。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he died and was given the posthumous title Wenqin.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he died and was given the posthumous title Wenqin (Diligent in Culture).

sentences.zh: 霨弱冠登第，大拜時年裁三十有四，風度端重，內介外和。

translations.literal: Li Wei passed the civil service examination in his early twenties; when he received the highest appointment he was only thirty-four, of dignified bearing, firm within yet gentle without.
translations.idiomatic: Li Wei passed the civil service examination before he came of age; when he received the highest ministerial appointment he was only thirty-four, of dignified bearing, firm within yet gentle in manner.

sentences.zh: 久居相位，尤嫺掌故，眷遇甚厚。

translations.literal: Having long held the chief ministership, he was especially well versed in precedent, and enjoyed very deep imperial favor.
translations.idiomatic: Having long held the chief ministership, he was especially well versed in precedent, and enjoyed very deep imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 四十九年，上追念前勞，超擢其孫工部主事敏啟為太常寺少卿。

translations.literal: In the forty-ninth year the emperor, recalling his past service, exceptionally promoted his grandson Minqi, a principal clerk in the Ministry of Works, to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-ninth year the emperor, recalling his past service, exceptionally promoted his grandson Minqi, a principal clerk in the Ministry of Works, to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 孫廷銓，初名廷鉉，字枚先，山東益都人。

translations.literal: Sun Tingquan, originally named Tingxuan, style name Meixian, a native of Yidu in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Tingquan, originally named Tingxuan, courtesy name Meixian, was a native of Yidu in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 明崇禎進士，任永平推官。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the Chongzhen reign of the Ming, he served as magistrate of criminal investigation in Yongping.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of the Chongzhen reign under the Ming, he served as investigating magistrate in Yongping.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，授天津推官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi he was appointed magistrate of criminal investigation in Tianjin.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shunzhi he was appointed investigating magistrate in Tianjin.

sentences.zh: 二年，以巡撫雷興薦，擢吏部主事，歷郎中。

translations.literal: In the second year, on the recommendation of Governor Lei Xing, he was promoted to a principal clerk in the Ministry of Personnel and rose through the ranks to director.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, on the recommendation of Governor Lei Xing, he was promoted to principal clerk in the Ministry of Personnel and rose through the ranks to director.

sentences.zh: 與曲沃衛周祚同官文選司，有聲於時。

translations.literal: Serving in the Ministry of Personnel in the Bureau of Appointments together with Wei Zhouzuo of Quwo, he enjoyed a fine reputation at the time.
translations.idiomatic: Serving in the Bureau of Appointments in the Ministry of Personnel together with Wei Zhouzuo of Quwo, he enjoyed a fine reputation at the time.

sentences.zh: 累遷左通政。

translations.literal: He was successively promoted to Vice Commissioner of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: He was successively promoted to Vice Commissioner of the Left.

sentences.zh: 十年，擢戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 以大學士洪承疇薦，召對。

translations.literal: On the recommendation of Grand Secretary Hong Chengchou, he was summoned for an audience.
translations.idiomatic: On the recommendation of Grand Secretary Hong Chengchou, he was summoned for an imperial audience.

sentences.zh: 尋坐事，罰俸，論告歸。

translations.literal: Before long he was punished by salary deduction for an offense and, on petition, returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was fined a portion of his salary for an offense and, on petition, returned home.

sentences.zh: 還朝，改兵部，擢尚書。

translations.literal: Returning to court, he was transferred to the Ministry of War and promoted to Minister.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned to court, he was transferred to the Ministry of War and promoted to Minister.

sentences.zh: 十三年，調戶部。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 廷銓以歲會無總錄，無以劑盈絀之宜，殫心綜覈，錢穀舊隸諸部者，各還所司，條貫釐然。

translations.literal: Sun Tingquan, finding that the annual fiscal summary had no overall ledger and no means to balance surplus and deficit, devoted himself to comprehensive review; funds and grain formerly subordinated to various ministries were each returned to their respective departments, and the system became clearly organized.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Tingquan found that the annual fiscal summary had no master ledger and no way to balance surplus and deficit; he devoted himself to a comprehensive review, returned funds and grain accounts that had been scattered among various ministries to their proper departments, and brought the system into clear order.

sentences.zh: 歲會之成自此始。

translations.literal: The completion of the annual summary began from this.
translations.idiomatic: The successful completion of the annual fiscal summary began from this.

sentences.zh: 十四年，疏言：「山東、河南荒田，請招民墾闢。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he memorialized: "For wasteland in Shandong and Henan, I request that people be recruited to open it for cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he memorialized: "For wasteland in Shandong and Henan, I ask that people be recruited to open it for cultivation.

sentences.zh: 其已熟者，清釐賦額，無使隱漏。」

translations.literal: For land already under cultivation, the tax quotas should be cleared and rectified so that nothing is concealed or omitted."
translations.idiomatic: For land already under cultivation, tax quotas should be cleared and rectified so that nothing is concealed or omitted."

sentences.zh: ​​上從其言。

translations.literal: The emperor followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor followed his advice.

sentences.zh: 十五年，調吏部，加太子太保。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel and granted the title Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel and was granted the title Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 十六年，諭獎其勤勞，加少保。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year the emperor commended his diligence and granted him the title Junior Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year the emperor commended his diligence and granted him the title Junior Guardian.

sentences.zh: 廷銓疏請復學道升補舊制，下所司集議，如廷銓請。

translations.literal: Sun Tingquan memorialized requesting restoration of the old system whereby educational commissioners made promotions and appointments; the matter was referred to the relevant offices for joint deliberation, and they followed Sun Tingquan's request.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Tingquan memorialized asking that the old system be restored whereby educational commissioners handled promotions and appointments; the matter was referred to the relevant offices for joint deliberation, and they adopted his proposal.

sentences.zh: 時吏部銓除，一事數例，吏胥因緣為奸。

translations.literal: At that time in the Ministry of Personnel appointments and dismissals for a single matter had several precedents, and clerks took advantage of this to practice fraud.
translations.idiomatic: At that time a single appointment matter in the Ministry of Personnel could be governed by several precedents, and clerks exploited the confusion to practice fraud.

sentences.zh: 給事中楊雍建、胡爾愷。

translations.literal: The supervising secretaries Yang Yongjian and Hu Erkai,
translations.idiomatic: The supervising secretaries Yang Yongjian and Hu Erkai,

sentences.zh: 黏本盛、孫際昌、王啟祚，御史許劭昕，交章發其弊，且劾廷銓因循為所蔽，奪加銜，罰俸。

translations.literal: Nian Bensheng, Sun Jichang, and Wang Qizuo, and Censor Xu Shaoxin, submitted successive memorials exposing these abuses, and also impeached Sun Tingquan for indulgence and being misled by them; his added title was stripped and his salary was fined.
translations.idiomatic: Nian Bensheng, Sun Jichang, and Wang Qizuo, and Censor Xu Shaoxin, submitted successive memorials exposing these abuses and also impeached Sun Tingquan for indulgence and being misled by the clerks; his added title was stripped and he was fined a portion of his salary.

sentences.zh: 十七年，疏言：「新闢邊疆員缺，督撫委用，即予實授，與部選之員，一體遷轉。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he memorialized: "For newly opened frontier posts, when governors and governors-general appoint officials and immediately grant substantive appointment, they are transferred on the same footing as those selected by the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he memorialized: "For newly opened frontier posts, when governors and governors-general appoint officials and immediately grant substantive appointment, they are transferred on the same footing as those selected by the ministry.

sentences.zh: 蒞事未久，輒移內地，請定為試署二年，乃予實授。」

translations.literal: Having taken office only briefly, they are soon moved to the interior; I request that it be fixed that they serve on probation for two years before substantive appointment is granted."
translations.idiomatic: Having served only briefly, they are soon moved to the interior; I ask that it be fixed that they serve on probation for two years before substantive appointment is granted."

sentences.zh: 又言：「司道不宜輕易，非大計處分及貪酷被糾者，遇降革，仍留任。」

translations.literal: He also said: "Provincial and circuit officials should not be lightly changed; except for those subject to major evaluation penalties or impeached for greed and cruelty, when demoted or dismissed in rank they should still be retained in office."
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Provincial and circuit officials should not be lightly replaced; except for those subject to major evaluation penalties or impeached for greed and cruelty, when demoted or dismissed in rank they should still be retained in office."

sentences.zh: 皆從之。

translations.literal: All were approved.
translations.idiomatic: All were approved.

sentences.zh: 又因旱，疏請寬考成，興屯政。

translations.literal: Because of drought he also memorialized requesting relaxation of performance evaluation and promotion of military colonies.
translations.idiomatic: Because of drought he also memorialized asking that performance evaluation be relaxed and military colonies be promoted.

sentences.zh: 上命兵部議屯政，而詢廷銓請寬考成議中有云「積資累薦，棄以一眚」語，何所指？

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the Ministry of War to deliberate on military colonies, and asked Sun Tingquan what was meant by the phrase in his memorial on relaxing evaluation, "long service and repeated recommendations, discarded for a single fault."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the Ministry of War to deliberate on military colonies, and asked Sun Tingquan what he meant by the phrase in his memorial on relaxing evaluation: "long service and repeated recommendations, discarded for a single fault."

sentences.zh: 廷銓言：「積疲州縣，久累人材，宜稍寬減觀後效，非為處分人員求免。」

translations.literal: Sun Tingquan said: "Prefectures and counties long worn down have for a long time burdened talented men; evaluation should be slightly relaxed and reduced to observe later results; this is not to seek exemption for punished personnel."
translations.idiomatic: Sun Tingquan said: "Prefectures and counties long worn down have for years burdened talented men; evaluation should be slightly relaxed so we may observe later results; this is not to seek exemption for punished officials."

sentences.zh: 世祖崩，二十七日制滿。

translations.literal: When the Shizu Emperor died, the twenty-seven-day mourning period was completed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Shunzhi Emperor died, the twenty-seven-day mourning period was completed.

sentences.zh: 廷銓發議尊皇太后為太皇太后，上所生母為皇太后，率九卿上請舉大禮疏。

translations.literal: Sun Tingquan initiated discussion to honor the Empress Dowager as Grand Empress Dowager and the emperor's birth mother as Empress Dowager, and led the Nine Ministers in submitting a memorial requesting the great rites.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Tingquan initiated discussion to honor the Empress Dowager as Grand Empress Dowager and the emperor's birth mother as Empress Dowager, and led the Nine Ministers in submitting a memorial requesting the great mourning rites.

sentences.zh: 及議大行皇帝諡號，廷銓曰：「大行皇帝龍興中土，混一六合，功業同於開創。

translations.literal: When they deliberated on the posthumous title of the late emperor, Sun Tingquan said: "The late emperor rose in the Central Plain and unified the realm; his achievements are equal to founding a dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: When they deliberated on the posthumous title of the late emperor, Sun Tingquan said: "The late emperor rose in the Central Plain and unified the realm; his achievements are equal to founding a dynasty.

sentences.zh: 宜謚為高皇帝。

translations.literal: He should be given the posthumous title Gaohuangdi.
translations.idiomatic: He should be given the posthumous title Gaohuangdi (High Emperor).

sentences.zh: 眾皆和之，而輔臣鼇拜持異議，遂定諡章皇帝。

translations.literal: All agreed, but the regent Oboi held a different view, and the posthumous title Zhanghuangdi was finally fixed.
translations.idiomatic: All agreed, but the regent Oboi held a different view, and the posthumous title Zhanghuangdi (Manifest Emperor) was finally fixed.

sentences.zh: 時太祖諡武皇帝，故廷銓議如是。

translations.literal: At that time Taizu had been given the posthumous title Wuhuangdi, and therefore Sun Tingquan argued as he did.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Taizu had been given the posthumous title Wuhuangdi (Martial Emperor), and therefore Sun Tingquan argued as he did.

sentences.zh: 時論頗歸之。

translations.literal: Contemporary opinion largely sided with him.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporary opinion largely sided with him.

sentences.zh: 康熙二年，拜秘書院大學士。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kangxi he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kangxi he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 奉職勤慎，終歲未嘗休沐。

translations.literal: He served diligently and cautiously and throughout the year never took leave for rest.
translations.idiomatic: He served with diligence and care and went the whole year without taking leave for rest.

sentences.zh: 逾年，以父母年老，解職歸養，閉戶卻掃，不與外事。

translations.literal: The following year, because his parents were old, he resigned his office to return home and support them, closed his doors and swept away visitors, and took no part in outside affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, because his parents were elderly, he resigned to return home and care for them, shut his doors to visitors, and took no part in outside affairs.

sentences.zh: 十三年，卒，諡文定。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he died and was given the posthumous title Wending.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he died and was given the posthumous title Wending (Settled in Culture).

sentences.zh: 杜立德，字純一，直隸寶坻人。

translations.literal: Du Lide, style name Chunyi, a native of Baodi in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Du Lide, courtesy name Chunyi, was a native of Baodi in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 明崇禎進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the Chongzhen reign of the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of the Chongzhen reign under the Ming.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，以順天巡撫宋權薦，授中書科中書。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi, on the recommendation of Shuntian Governor Song Quan, he was appointed secretary in the Secretariat Section.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shunzhi, on the recommendation of Shuntian Governor Song Quan, he was appointed secretary in the Secretariat Section.

sentences.zh: 二年，考選戶科給事中。

translations.literal: In the second year he was selected by examination as supervising secretary in the Revenue Section.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was selected by examination as supervising secretary in the Revenue Section.

sentences.zh: 疏陳：「治平之道有三：一曰敬天。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "The way to good government has three parts: first, reverence for Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "The way to good government has three parts: first, reverence for Heaven.

sentences.zh: 君為天之子，當修省以迓天休。

translations.literal: The ruler is Heaven's son and should cultivate himself and examine his conduct to welcome Heaven's favor.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler is Heaven's son and should cultivate himself and examine his conduct to welcome Heaven's favor.

sentences.zh: 今秦、晉、燕畿水旱風雹，天心示警。

translations.literal: Now in Qin, Jin, and the capital region there are floods, droughts, and hailstorms; Heaven's heart shows warning.
translations.idiomatic: Now in Shaanxi, Shanxi, and the capital region there are floods, droughts, and hailstorms; Heaven is showing its warning.

sentences.zh: 凡開誠佈公，懋德敦行，皆敬天事也。

translations.literal: All such matters as opening one's heart and showing fairness, and encouraging virtue and earnest conduct, are acts of reverence for Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: All such matters as opening one's heart and acting with fairness, and encouraging virtue and earnest conduct, are acts of reverence for Heaven.

sentences.zh: 一曰法古。

translations.literal: Second, following antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Second, following antiquity.

sentences.zh: 古者事之鑑，是非定於一時，法則昭於百代。

translations.literal: Antiquity is the mirror of affairs; right and wrong are fixed in a single age, but law shines forth for a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: Antiquity is the mirror of affairs; right and wrong may be fixed in a single age, but law shines forth for a hundred generations.

sentences.zh: 故合經而後能權，遵法而後能創。

translations.literal: Therefore only after conforming to the classics can one exercise discretion; only after following law can one innovate.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore only after conforming to the classics can one exercise discretion; only after following law can one innovate.

sentences.zh: 凡建學明倫，立綱陳紀，皆法古事也。

translations.literal: All such matters as establishing schools and clarifying human relations, and setting forth principles and laying down regulations, are acts of following antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: All such matters as establishing schools and clarifying human relations, and setting forth principles and laying down regulations, are acts of following antiquity.

sentences.zh: 一曰愛人。

translations.literal: Third, loving the people.
translations.idiomatic: Third, loving the people.

sentences.zh: 自大臣以至百姓，宜一視同仁。

translations.literal: From great ministers down to the common people, all should be treated with equal benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: From great ministers down to the common people, all should be treated with equal benevolence.

sentences.zh: 且無論新舊，悉存棄短取長之心。

translations.literal: Moreover, whether old or new subjects, one should always keep the mind of discarding the short and taking the long.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, whether old or new subjects, one should always keep the mind of discarding weaknesses and taking strengths.

sentences.zh: 凡親賢納諫，尚德緩刑，皆愛人事也。」

translations.literal: All such matters as drawing near the worthy and accepting remonstrance, honoring virtue and moderating punishments, are acts of loving the people.
translations.idiomatic: All such matters as drawing near the worthy and accepting remonstrance, honoring virtue and moderating punishments, are acts of loving the people.

sentences.zh: 上以其有裨治理，深嘉納之。

translations.literal: The emperor, finding this beneficial to governance, deeply praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, finding this beneficial to governance, deeply praised and accepted it.

sentences.zh: 又累疏言：「牧民之官，宜久任以驗成功。

translations.literal: He also submitted successive memorials saying: "Officials who shepherd the people should serve long terms to verify their success.
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted successive memorials saying: "Officials who shepherd the people should serve long terms to verify their success.

sentences.zh: 凡遇賑蠲，宜分別款項，豫行頒示，使小民咸喻，胥吏不能為奸。」

translations.literal: Whenever relief or tax remission is granted, the items should be distinguished and announced in advance, so that the common people all understand and clerks cannot practice fraud."
translations.idiomatic: Whenever relief or tax remission is granted, the items should be distinguished and announced in advance, so that common people all understand and clerks cannot practice fraud."

sentences.zh: 「條編法簡易便民。

translations.literal: The single-whip method is simple and convenient for the people.
translations.idiomatic: The single-whip method is simple and convenient for the people.

sentences.zh: 軍興草豆無定額，宜敕部定價值，使民先事為備。」

translations.literal: When the army is raised, fodder and grain have no fixed quotas; the ministry should be ordered to fix prices so that the people may prepare in advance."
translations.idiomatic: When the army is raised, fodder and grain have no fixed quotas; the ministry should be ordered to fix prices so that the people may prepare in advance."

sentences.zh: 皆下部議行。

translations.literal: All were referred to the ministries for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: All were referred to the ministries for deliberation and implementation.

sentences.zh: 累遷戶科都給事中。

translations.literal: He was successively promoted to Chief Supervising Secretary of the Revenue Section.
translations.idiomatic: He was successively promoted to Chief Supervising Secretary of the Revenue Section.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「漕運叢弊，今漕臣庫禮搜獲運官使費冊三十本送部。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "The grain transport system is rife with abuses; now Transport Commissioner Ku Li has searched out and seized thirty account books of transport officials' expenses and sent them to the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "The grain transport system is rife with abuses; now Transport Commissioner Ku Li has searched out and seized thirty account books of transport officials' expenses and sent them to the ministry.

sentences.zh: 請敕窮究，以釐姦弊。」

translations.literal: I request an imperial order for thorough investigation to rectify fraud and abuse."
translations.idiomatic: I request an imperial order for thorough investigation to rectify fraud and abuse."

sentences.zh: 再遷吏科都給事中。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to Chief Supervising Secretary of the Personnel Section.
translations.idiomatic: He was again promoted to Chief Supervising Secretary of the Personnel Section.

sentences.zh: 八年，疏請舉行經筵，擇廷臣經明行修者為講官，以裨聖治；

translations.literal: In the eighth year he memorialized requesting that the classics lecture be held, and that court officials distinguished in the classics and upright in conduct be chosen as lecturers to benefit sagely governance;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he memorialized asking that the imperial classics lecture be held, and that court officials distinguished in the classics and upright in conduct be chosen as lecturers to benefit the emperor's governance;

sentences.zh: 又請定朝期，肅禁地，杜加派。

translations.literal: he also requested fixing court schedules, enforcing the forbidden precinct, and stopping extra levies.
translations.idiomatic: he also asked that court schedules be fixed, the forbidden precinct be enforced, and extra levies be stopped.

sentences.zh: 上甚韙之。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor greatly approved.

sentences.zh: 初，睿親王多爾袞攝政，給事中許作梅，御史吳達、李森先、桑芸等交章劾大學士馮銓姦貪狀，疏上旬日，未下廷議。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Prince Regent Dorgon held power, the supervising secretaries Xu Zuomei and the censors Wu Da, Li Senxian, Sang Yun, and others submitted successive memorials impeaching Grand Secretary Feng Quan for corruption and greed; the memorials had been on the throne for ten days without being referred to court deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the Prince Regent Dorgon held power, Supervising Secretary Xu Zuomei and Censors Wu Da, Li Senxian, Sang Yun, and others submitted successive memorials impeaching Grand Secretary Feng Quan for corruption and greed; the memorials had been before the throne for ten days without being referred to court deliberation.

sentences.zh: 立德請令滿、漢大臣集議，以伸公論，鼓直言之氣；

translations.literal: Lide requested that Manchu and Han grand ministers be ordered to deliberate jointly, to give full play to public opinion and encourage the spirit of frank speech;
translations.idiomatic: Lide asked that Manchu and Han grand ministers be ordered to deliberate jointly, to give full play to public opinion and encourage frank speech;

sentences.zh: 並及馬士英、阮大鋮、宋企郊等，在前朝或納賄招權，或煽惡流毒，今並逋逃，宜急捕誅，以彰法紀。

translations.literal: and also concerning Ma Shiying, Ruan Dacheng, Song Qijiao, and others, who in the previous dynasty either accepted bribes and gathered power or stirred up evil and spread poison—all now fugitives—they should be urgently captured and executed to manifest the law.
translations.idiomatic: and also concerning Ma Shiying, Ruan Dacheng, Song Qijiao, and others, who under the previous dynasty either accepted bribes and gathered power or stirred up evil and spread poison—all now fugitives—who should be urgently captured and executed to uphold the law.

sentences.zh: 下刑部，以事在赦前，寢其議。

translations.literal: The matter was referred to the Ministry of Punishments; because the offenses occurred before an amnesty, the proposal was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was referred to the Ministry of Punishments; because the offenses occurred before an amnesty, the proposal was shelved.

sentences.zh: 世祖親政，銓既黜，立德因言作梅等前以劾銓為所切齒，又僉都御史趙開心素為銓所忌，相繼構陷去官，乞矜察。

translations.literal: When the Shizu Emperor took power in person and Quan was dismissed, Lide said that Zuomei and others had earlier been bitterly resented by Quan for impeaching him, and that Vice Censor-in-Chief Zhao Kaixin had long been hated by Quan and was successively framed and driven from office; he begged compassionate review.
translations.idiomatic: When the Shunzhi Emperor took power in person and Quan was dismissed, Lide said that Zuomei and others had earlier been bitterly resented by Quan for impeaching him, and that Vice Censor-in-Chief Zhao Kaixin had long been hated by Quan and was successively framed and driven from office; he begged compassionate review.

sentences.zh: 由是開心等俱起用。

translations.literal: Thereupon Kaixin and the others were all reappointed.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Kaixin and the others were all reappointed.

sentences.zh: 立德尋遷太常寺少卿，超擢工部侍郎，調兵部。

translations.literal: Lide was soon transferred to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, exceptionally promoted to Vice Minister of Works, and transferred to the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Lide was soon transferred to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, exceptionally promoted to Vice Minister of Works, and transferred to the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 畿輔水災，奉詔賑濟大名，全活甚眾。

translations.literal: When the capital region suffered flood, by imperial order he provided relief in Daming and saved a great many lives.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital region suffered flooding, by imperial order he provided relief in Daming and saved a great many lives.

sentences.zh: 再調吏部，以父憂去。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to the Ministry of Personnel and left office on account of his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: He was again transferred to the Ministry of Personnel and left office to mourn his father.

sentences.zh: 坐兵部任詿誤，鐫秩調用。

translations.literal: Because of an error in his duties at the Ministry of War, he was demoted in rank and transferred.
translations.idiomatic: Because of an error in his duties at the Ministry of War, he was demoted in rank and transferred.

sentences.zh: 服闋，除太僕寺卿，擢刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: When mourning was completed, he was appointed Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud and promoted to Vice Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning was completed, he was appointed Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud and promoted to Vice Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 十六年，加太子少保銜。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was granted the title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was granted the title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 領侍衛內大臣額爾克岱青家奴縛侍衛誣訴，部議罪侍衛，下內大臣索尼等察實，立德奪加銜。

translations.literal: A bondservant of the Inner Minister Erke Daiqing, who headed the guards, bound a guard and lodged a false accusation; the ministry deliberated and punished the guard, but when Inner Ministers Sony and others investigated the facts, Lide was stripped of his added title.
translations.idiomatic: A bondservant of Inner Minister Erke Daiqing, who headed the guards, bound a guard and lodged a false accusation; the ministry deliberated and punished the guard, but when Inner Ministers Sony and others investigated the facts, Lide was stripped of his added title.

sentences.zh: 十六年，擢尚書。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was promoted to Minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was promoted to Minister.

sentences.zh: 立德治獄仁恕，上聞其用法平，深嘉之。

translations.literal: Lide handled cases with benevolence and forbearance; the emperor heard that his application of the law was even-handed and deeply praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Lide handled cases with benevolence and forbearance; the emperor heard that his application of the law was even-handed and deeply praised him.

sentences.zh: 嘗入對，既出，上顧左右曰：「此新授刑部尚書杜立德也！

translations.literal: Once after he had entered for an audience and left, the emperor turned to those beside him and said: "This is the newly appointed Minister of Punishments Du Lide!
translations.idiomatic: Once after he had entered for an audience and left, the emperor turned to those beside him and said: "This is the newly appointed Minister of Punishments Du Lide!

sentences.zh: 不貪一錢，亦不妄殺一人。」

translations.literal: He does not covet a single coin, nor does he kill a person without cause."
translations.idiomatic: He does not covet a single coin, nor does he kill a person without cause."

sentences.zh: 康熙元年，調戶部。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kangxi he was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kangxi he was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 考滿，復加太子少保。

translations.literal: When his evaluation period was completed, he was again granted the title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When his evaluation period was completed, he was again granted the title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 三年，調吏部。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 八年，拜國史院大學士。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 聖祖親政，乾清宮成，擇日臨御，欽天監奏吉神在隅，不宜從中門入。

translations.literal: When the Kangxi Emperor took power in person, the Palace of Heavenly Purity was completed, and a day was chosen for him to take up residence; the Directorate of Astronomy reported that the auspicious spirit was in a corner and that he should not enter by the central gate.
translations.idiomatic: When the Kangxi Emperor took power in person, the Palace of Heavenly Purity was completed, and a day was chosen for him to take up residence; the Directorate of Astronomy reported that the auspicious spirit was in a corner and that he should not enter by the central gate.

sentences.zh: 立德言：「紫微帝星所在，吉神拱向。

translations.literal: Lide said: "The Purple Forbidden Star, the seat of the imperial star, is where the auspicious spirits gather and face.
translations.idiomatic: Lide said: "The Purple Forbidden Star, the seat of the imperial star, is where the auspicious spirits gather and face.

sentences.zh: 皇上遷正新宮，臣庶觀瞻，應從中門入。

translations.literal: When Your Majesty moves to the new palace, officials and common people will look on; you should enter by the central gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty moves to the new palace, officials and common people will look on; you should enter by the central gate.

sentences.zh: 監臣所奏非是。」

translations.literal: What the directorate officials reported is not correct."
translations.idiomatic: What the directorate officials reported is not correct."

sentences.zh: 上從其言。

translations.literal: The emperor followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor followed his advice.

sentences.zh: 九年，改保和殿大學士，兼禮部尚書，進太子太傅。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was made Grand Secretary of the Hall of Preserving Harmony, concurrently Minister of Rites, and promoted to Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was made Grand Secretary of the Hall of Preserving Harmony, concurrently served as Minister of Rites, and was promoted to Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 三籓事起，立德與李霨、馮溥參預機務。

translations.literal: When the Three Feudatories rebellion arose, Lide, together with Li Wei and Feng Pu, took part in deciding affairs of state.
translations.idiomatic: When the Three Feudatories rebellion arose, Lide, together with Li Wei and Feng Pu, took part in deciding affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 從容整暇，中外相安。

translations.literal: Composed and unhurried, within and without the court were at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Composed and unhurried, they kept the court and the realm at ease.

sentences.zh: 廣東平，所司具正雜賦稅之數以聞。

translations.literal: When Guangdong was pacified, the responsible offices submitted the figures for regular and miscellaneous taxes for report.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangdong was pacified, the responsible offices submitted the figures for regular and miscellaneous taxes for report.

sentences.zh: 立德言：「廣東雜稅多尚之信所加，為民間大累，非朝廷正額。

translations.literal: Lide said: "Most of Guangdong's miscellaneous taxes were added by Shang Zhixin and are a great burden on the people; they are not regular quotas of the court.
translations.idiomatic: Lide said: "Most of Guangdong's miscellaneous taxes were added by Shang Zhixin and are a great burden on the people; they are not regular quotas of the court.

sentences.zh: 今變亂甫定，宜與民休息。

translations.literal: Now that rebellion has just been settled, the people should be allowed to rest.
translations.idiomatic: Now that rebellion has just been settled, the people should be allowed to rest.

sentences.zh: 其除之便。」

translations.literal: It would be best to abolish them."
translations.idiomatic: It would be best to abolish them."

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor followed his advice.

sentences.zh: 十八年，自陳乞休。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he petitioned on his own account to retire.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he petitioned on his own account to retire.

sentences.zh: 其秋地震，復請罷，詔輒慰留。

translations.literal: That autumn there was an earthquake; he again requested to resign, but each time an edict comforted him and kept him in office.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn there was an earthquake; he again requested to resign, but each time an edict comforted him and kept him in office.

sentences.zh: 雲南平，議頒恩赦，立德告病未與議，遣大臣持詔旨就其家諮詢，俟還奏乃下詔。

translations.literal: When Yunnan was pacified, an amnesty was discussed; Lide reported illness and did not take part in the deliberation; the emperor sent a grand minister with the edict draft to consult him at his home, and only after the minister returned and reported was the edict issued.
translations.idiomatic: When Yunnan was pacified, an amnesty was discussed; Lide reported illness and did not take part in the deliberation; the emperor sent a grand minister with the edict draft to consult him at his home, and only after the minister returned and reported was the edict issued.

sentences.zh: 一日，上顧閣臣，謂在廷諸臣誰堪大用者，立德面疏數人以對。

translations.literal: One day the emperor looked at the grand secretaries and asked which officials at court were fit for great employment; Lide privately listed several men in reply.
translations.idiomatic: One day the emperor looked at the grand secretaries and asked which officials at court were fit for great employment; Lide privately listed several men in reply.

sentences.zh: 比退，人訝其不稍引嫌，答曰：「自筮仕以來，惟此心可邀帝鑑。

translations.literal: When he withdrew, people were surprised that he did not hold back out of scruple; he replied: "Since I entered office, only this heart can invite the emperor's discernment.
translations.idiomatic: When he withdrew, people were surprised that he did not hold back out of scruple; he replied: "Since I entered office, only this heart can invite the emperor's discernment.

sentences.zh: 他非所計也。」

translations.literal: Other things are not what I calculate."
translations.idiomatic: Other things are not what I calculate."

sentences.zh: 二十一年夏，复乞休，上許之，賜御製詩及「怡情洛社」篆章，馳驛遣行人護歸。

translations.literal: In the summer of the twenty-first year he again petitioned to retire; the emperor granted it, bestowed an imperial poem and a seal inscribed "Finding Joy in the Lu Community," and dispatched an imperial messenger by post to escort him home.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the twenty-first year he again petitioned to retire; the emperor granted it, bestowed an imperial poem and a seal inscribed "Finding Joy in the Lu Community," and dispatched an imperial messenger by post to escort him home.

sentences.zh: 太宗實錄成，進太子太師，賜銀幣、鞍馬。

translations.literal: When the Veritable Records of Taizong were completed, he was promoted to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent and granted silver coins and saddle horses.
translations.idiomatic: When the Veritable Records of Taizong were completed, he was promoted to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent and granted silver coins and saddle horses.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，太皇太后喪，立德詣京師哭臨，上念其老病不任拜起，命學士張英扶掖以行，慰勞甚至。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, at the Grand Empress Dowager's death, Lide came to the capital to mourn; the emperor, mindful that he was old and ill and unable to perform the bows and risings, ordered Bachelor Zhang Ying to support him as he walked and comforted him with exceptional kindness.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year, at the Grand Empress Dowager's death, Lide came to the capital to mourn; the emperor, mindful that he was old and ill and unable to perform the bows and risings, ordered Bachelor Zhang Ying to support him as he walked and comforted him with exceptional kindness.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，卒，年八十一，上聞，諭大學士曰：「杜立德秉性厚重，行事正大。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year he died at the age of eighty-one; when the emperor heard, he told the grand secretaries: "Du Lide was by nature solid and weighty, and upright in conduct.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year he died at the age of eighty-one; when the emperor heard, he told the grand secretaries: "Du Lide was by nature solid and weighty, and upright in conduct.

sentences.zh: 直言敷奏，不肯苟隨同列。

translations.literal: He spoke frankly in memorials and would not lightly follow his colleagues.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke frankly in memorials and would not lightly follow his colleagues.

sentences.zh: 可謂賢臣！」

translations.literal: He may be called a worthy minister!"
translations.idiomatic: He may be called a worthy minister!"

sentences.zh: 賜祭葬如禮，諡文端。

translations.literal: Sacrificial and burial honors were granted according to ritual, and he was given the posthumous title Wenduan.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrificial and burial honors were granted according to ritual, and he was given the posthumous title Wenduan (Correct in Culture).

sentences.zh: 三十九年，帝南巡，其子恭俊迎駕三河，上問立德葬所，手書「永言惟舊」四字賜之，命揭諸阡。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year, when the emperor toured the south, his son Gongjun met the imperial procession at Sanhe; the emperor asked where Lide was buried, personally wrote the four characters "Forever remembering the old," bestowed them, and ordered them displayed at the tomb path.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-ninth year, when the emperor toured the south, his son Gongjun met the imperial procession at Sanhe; the emperor asked where Lide was buried, personally wrote the four characters "Forever remembering the old," bestowed them, and ordered them displayed at the tomb path.

sentences.zh: 恭俊官廣信知府，好義，善濟人急。

translations.literal: Gongjun served as prefect of Guangxin, loved righteousness, and was good at relieving people in urgent need.
translations.idiomatic: Gongjun served as prefect of Guangxin, loved righteousness, and was good at relieving people in urgent need.

sentences.zh: 馮溥，字孔博，山東益都人。

translations.literal: Feng Pu, style name Kongbo, a native of Yidu in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Pu, courtesy name Kongbo, was a native of Yidu in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 順治三年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the third year of Shunzhi, he was selected as a Hanlin bachelor and appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of the third year of Shunzhi, he was selected as a Hanlin bachelor and appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 累遷秘書院侍讀學士，直講經筵。

translations.literal: He was successively promoted to Reader of the Secretariat and served regularly at the classics lecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was successively promoted to Reader of the Secretariat and served regularly at the imperial classics lecture.

sentences.zh: 世祖幸內院，顧大學士曰：「朕視馮溥乃真翰林也！」

translations.literal: When the Shizu Emperor visited the inner court, he turned to the grand secretaries and said: "In my view Feng Pu is a true Hanlin scholar!"
translations.idiomatic: When the Shunzhi Emperor visited the inner court, he turned to the grand secretaries and said: "In my view Feng Pu is a true Hanlin scholar!"

sentences.zh: 十六年，擢吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was promoted to Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was promoted to Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 會各省學道缺，部郎不足，以知府補之。

translations.literal: When educational commissioner posts in the provinces were vacant and there were not enough directors in the ministry, prefects were appointed to fill them.
translations.idiomatic: When educational commissioner posts in the provinces were vacant and there were not enough directors in the ministry, prefects were appointed to fill them.

sentences.zh: 已，會禮部議奏，時尚書孫廷銓、侍郎石申並乞假；

translations.literal: Later, when the Ministry of Rites met to deliberate and report, at that time Minister Sun Tingquan and Vice Minister Shi Shen were both on leave;
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the Ministry of Rites met to deliberate and report, at that time Minister Sun Tingquan and Vice Minister Shi Shen were both on leave;

sentences.zh: 給事中張維赤因劾溥徇私，溥疏辨。

translations.literal: the supervising secretary Zhang Weichi impeached Pu for favoritism, and Pu memorialized in defense.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Zhang Weichi impeached Pu for favoritism, and Pu memorialized in defense.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕知溥不為也！」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I know Pu would not do such a thing!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "I know Pu would not do such a thing!"

sentences.zh: 置勿問。

translations.literal: The matter was set aside and not pursued.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was set aside and not pursued.

sentences.zh: 明年，京官三品以上自陳，忽嚴旨黜滿尚書科爾坤及兩侍郎，獨留漢官在部。

translations.literal: The next year, when capital officials of the third rank and above submitted self-evaluations, a sudden stern edict dismissed the Manchu Minister Ke'erkun and two vice ministers, leaving only Han officials in the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, when capital officials of the third rank and above submitted self-evaluations, a sudden stern edict dismissed the Manchu Minister Ke'erkun and two vice ministers, leaving only Han officials in the ministry.

sentences.zh: 溥與廷銓疏言：「部事滿、漢同治，今滿臣得罪，漢臣安得免，乞並黜。」

translations.literal: Pu and Tingquan memorialized: "Ministry affairs are administered jointly by Manchu and Han; now that Manchu ministers have been punished, how can Han ministers be exempt? We beg to be dismissed together."
translations.idiomatic: Pu and Tingquan memorialized: "Ministry affairs are administered jointly by Manchu and Han; now that Manchu ministers have been punished, how can Han ministers be exempt? We beg to be dismissed together."

sentences.zh: 詔供職如故。

translations.literal: An edict ordered them to continue in office as before.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered them to continue in office as before.

sentences.zh: 康熙初，停各省巡按，議每省遣大臣二人廉察督撫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kangxi, when provincial surveillance commissioners were abolished, it was proposed that each province send two grand ministers to inspect governors and governors-general.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Kangxi, when provincial surveillance commissioners were abolished, it was proposed that each province send two grand ministers to inspect governors and governors-general.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書阿思哈、侍郎泰必圖議設公廨，頒冊印。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Asiha and Vice Minister Taibitu proposed establishing public offices and issuing registers and seals.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Asiha and Vice Minister Taibitu proposed establishing public offices and issuing registers and seals.

sentences.zh: 溥謂：「國家設督撫，皆重臣。

translations.literal: Pu said: "The state appoints governors and governors-general, all of them weighty ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Pu said: "The state appoints governors and governors-general, all of them weighty ministers.

sentences.zh: 今謂不可信，復遣兩大臣監之。

translations.literal: Now to say they cannot be trusted and to send two more grand ministers to supervise them—
translations.idiomatic: Now to say they cannot be trusted and to send two more grand ministers to supervise them.

sentences.zh: 權既太重，勢復相軋，保無屬吏仰承左右啟隙端？」

translations.literal: Authority would be too heavy and power would again clash; can we be sure that subordinate officials would not look to those on the left and right and open rifts?"
translations.idiomatic: Authority would be too heavy and power would again clash; can we be sure that subordinate officials would not look to those on the left and right and open rifts?"

sentences.zh: 泰必圖性暴伉，聞溥言，恚，瞋目攘臂起。

translations.literal: Taibitu was by nature violent and overbearing; hearing Pu's words, he was enraged, glared, and rose with arms flung wide.
translations.idiomatic: Taibitu was by nature violent and overbearing; hearing Pu's words, he was enraged, glared, and rose with arms flung wide.

sentences.zh: 溥徐曰：「會議也，獨不容吾兩議耶？

translations.literal: Pu said calmly: "This is a conference; are we alone not allowed to offer two opinions?
translations.idiomatic: Pu said calmly: "This is a conference; are we alone not allowed to offer two opinions?

sentences.zh: 且可否自有上裁，豈敢專主？」

translations.literal: Moreover, approval or rejection rests with the emperor's decision; how would we dare to decide on our own?"
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, approval or rejection rests with the emperor's decision; how would we dare to decide on our own?"

sentences.zh: 疏入，上然溥言，事遂寢。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor agreed with Pu's view and the matter was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor agreed with Pu's view and the matter was shelved.

sentences.zh: 御史李秀以考績黜，後夤緣得復官，劾溥為故相劉正宗黨，主銓時違例徇私，溥疏辨，嚴旨責秀誣訐。

translations.literal: Censor Li Xiu had been dismissed after evaluation but later gained reinstatement through connections; he impeached Pu as a partisan of the former chief minister Liu Zhengzong and for violating regulations and showing favoritism when he headed appointments; Pu memorialized in defense, and a stern edict rebuked Xiu for slander.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Li Xiu had been dismissed after evaluation but later gained reinstatement through connections; he impeached Pu as a partisan of the former chief minister Liu Zhengzong and for violating regulations and showing favoritism when he headed appointments; Pu memorialized in defense, and a stern edict rebuked Xiu for slander.

sentences.zh: 六年，遷左都御史。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to Censor-in-Chief of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was transferred to Censor-in-Chief of the Left.

sentences.zh: 內閣有紅本，已發科鈔，輔臣鼇拜取回改批。

translations.literal: In the Grand Secretariat there was a red draft that had already been sent to the ministries for copying; the regent Oboi took it back and altered the endorsement.
translations.idiomatic: In the Grand Secretariat there was a red draft that had already been sent to the ministries for copying; the regent Oboi took it back and altered the endorsement.

sentences.zh: 溥抗言：「本章既批發，不便更改。」

translations.literal: Pu protested: "Since this memorial has already been endorsed and issued, it should not be changed."
translations.idiomatic: Pu protested: "Since this memorial has already been endorsed and issued, it should not be changed."

sentences.zh: 鼇拜欲罪之，上直溥，戒輔臣詳慎。

translations.literal: Oboi wished to punish him, but the emperor supported Pu and admonished the regents to be careful and thorough.
translations.idiomatic: Oboi wished to punish him, but the emperor supported Pu and admonished the regents to be careful and thorough.

sentences.zh: 盛京工部侍郎缺，已會推，奉旨以規避者多，不旬日三易其人。

translations.literal: When the vice ministership in the Ministry of Works at Mukden fell vacant, candidates had already been jointly recommended, but an edict said that too many were evading the post; within ten days the appointee was changed three times.
translations.idiomatic: When the vice ministership in the Ministry of Works at Mukden fell vacant, candidates had already been jointly recommended, but an edict said that too many were evading the post; within ten days the appointee was changed three times.

sentences.zh: 溥疏言：「王言不宜反汗，當慎重於未有旨之先，不當更移於已奉旨之後。」

translations.literal: Pu memorialized: "Imperial words should not be reversed; deliberation should be careful before an edict is issued, and should not be changed after an edict has already been received."
translations.idiomatic: Pu memorialized: "Imperial words should not be reversed; deliberation should be careful before an edict is issued, and should not be changed after an edict has already been received."

sentences.zh: 首輔班布爾善寢其奏，上聞，取溥疏覽之，稱善，飭部施行。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Banbu'ershan shelved the memorial, but when the emperor heard of it he had Pu's memorial brought for review, praised it, and ordered the ministry to implement it.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Banbu'ershan shelved the memorial, but when the emperor heard of it he had Pu's memorial brought for review, praised it, and ordered the ministry to implement it.

sentences.zh: 八年夏，旱，應詔陳言，請省刑薄稅。

translations.literal: In the summer of the eighth year, during drought, in response to an edict inviting opinion, he requested lighter punishments and reduced taxes.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the eighth year, during drought, in response to an edict inviting opinion, he requested lighter punishments and reduced taxes.

sentences.zh: 略謂：「古者罪人不孥，今一事牽連佐證，或數人，或數十人。

translations.literal: He said in summary: "In antiquity guilt did not extend to families; today a single case may implicate witnesses and associates, sometimes several people, sometimes several tens.
translations.idiomatic: He said in summary: "In antiquity guilt did not extend to families; today a single case may implicate witnesses and associates, sometimes several people, sometimes several tens.

sentences.zh: 往往本犯尚未審明，而被累致死者已多。

translations.literal: Often before the principal offender has even been clearly tried, many of those implicated have already died.
translations.idiomatic: Often before the principal offender has even been clearly tried, many of those implicated have already died.

sentences.zh: 且或遲至七八年尚未結案，遂致力穡供稅之人，拋家失業。

translations.literal: Moreover, cases may drag on seven or eight years without conclusion, so that people who labor in the fields and pay taxes abandon their homes and lose their livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, cases may drag on seven or eight years without conclusion, so that people who labor in the fields and pay taxes abandon their homes and lose their livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 請敕部嚴禁。

translations.literal: I request that the ministries be ordered to forbid this strictly.
translations.idiomatic: I request that the ministries be ordered to forbid this strictly.

sentences.zh: 百姓之財，不過取之田畝。

translations.literal: The people's wealth comes only from the fields.
translations.idiomatic: The people's wealth comes only from the fields.

sentences.zh: 今正月已開徵，舊稅之逋甫償，新歲之田未種，錢糧從何辦納？

translations.literal: Now collection has already begun in the first month; arrears of old taxes have just been paid, and the fields of the new year are not yet planted—how are grain taxes to be paid?
translations.idiomatic: Now collection has already begun in the first month; arrears of old taxes have just been paid, and the fields of the new year are not yet planted—how are grain taxes to be paid?

sentences.zh: 請敕部酌議。

translations.literal: I request that the ministries be ordered to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: I request that the ministries be ordered to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 自後徵賦，緩待夏秋。」

translations.literal: Henceforth tax collection should wait until summer and autumn."
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth tax collection should wait until summer and autumn."

sentences.zh: 下戶、刑二部議。

translations.literal: The matter was referred to the Ministries of Revenue and Punishments for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was referred to the Ministries of Revenue and Punishments for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 刑部議，承審強盜、人命重案，限一年速結，不得牽累無辜，督撫及承審官隱漏遲延皆有罰。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Punishments deliberated that robbery and homicide cases under trial should be concluded within one year, that the innocent must not be implicated, and that governors and trial officials who concealed, omitted, or delayed would all be punished.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Punishments deliberated that robbery and homicide cases under trial should be concluded within one year, that the innocent must not be implicated, and that governors and trial officials who concealed, omitted, or delayed would all be punished.

sentences.zh: 戶部議，春季兵餉不能待至夏秋，仍舊例便。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Revenue deliberated that spring military pay could not wait until summer and autumn, and that the old practice should stand.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Revenue deliberated that spring military pay could not wait until summer and autumn, and that the old practice should stand.

sentences.zh: 得旨，俟國用充足，戶部奏請更定。

translations.literal: An edict was received: when state revenue is ample, the Ministry of Revenue should memorialize requesting revision.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was received: when state revenue is ample, the Ministry of Revenue should memorialize requesting revision.

sentences.zh: 戶部吏陳一魁冒領清苑等縣錢糧事發，溥言：「錢糧者百姓之脂膏也，其已輸在官，則朝廷之帑藏也。

translations.literal: When Ministry of Revenue clerk Chen Yikui was found to have falsely claimed grain taxes from Qingyuan and other counties, Pu said: "Grain taxes are the fat and cream of the people; once paid into the government, they are the treasury of the court.
translations.idiomatic: When Ministry of Revenue clerk Chen Yikui was found to have falsely claimed grain taxes from Qingyuan and other counties, Pu said: "Grain taxes are the fat and cream of the people; once paid into the government, they are the treasury of the court.

sentences.zh: 若任胥吏侵盜，職掌謂何？

translations.literal: If clerks are allowed to embezzle, what becomes of official responsibility?
translations.idiomatic: If clerks are allowed to embezzle, what becomes of official responsibility?

sentences.zh: 請嚴定所司處分，懲前毖後。」

translations.literal: I request that the responsible offices fix penalties strictly, punishing the past to guard the future."」
translations.idiomatic: I request that the responsible offices fix penalties strictly, punishing the past to guard the future."」

sentences.zh: 擢刑部尚書。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: and was promoted to Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 十年，拜文華殿大學士。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Wenhua Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, he received appointment as Grand Secretary of the Wenhua Hall.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「直隸、山東、河南、山西、陝西米麥豐收，穀價每鬥值銀三四分。

translations.literal: In a memorial he said: "In Zhili, Shandong, Henan, Shanxi, and Shaanxi, rice and wheat harvests are abundant, and grain prices stand at three or four fen of silver per dou.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial stating: "Zhili, Shandong, Henan, Shanxi, and Shaanxi have enjoyed bountiful harvests of rice and wheat, with grain selling for only three or four fen of silver per dou.

sentences.zh: 當此豐稔之時，宜廣積貯，以備凶年。」

translations.literal: At such a time of bumper harvest, it is fitting to store grain widely, to prepare for years of famine."
translations.idiomatic: In times of such plenty, the state ought to build up reserves against future famine."

sentences.zh: 先是，溥以衰病累疏乞休，上曰：「卿六十四歲，未衰也，俟七十乃休耳。」

translations.literal: Previously, Pu, citing decline and illness, repeatedly memorialized asking to retire. The emperor said: "You are sixty-four years old—not yet aged. Wait until seventy before retiring."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Pu had repeatedly petitioned to retire on grounds of age and illness. The emperor replied: "You are only sixty-four—you are not yet old. You may retire when you reach seventy."

sentences.zh: 自吳三桂反，軍事旁午，乃不敢復言。

translations.literal: From the time Wu Sangui rebelled, military affairs came from all sides, and he dared not speak of it again.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu Sangui rose in rebellion and military crises pressed in from every direction, he did not dare raise the matter again.

sentences.zh: 十四年，建儲禮成，內閣議恩赦，滿大臣以八旗逃人應不赦，溥不可，遂兩議以進。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, when the investiture ceremony was completed, the Grand Secretariat deliberated on an amnesty. Manchu ministers held that runaway bannermen should not be pardoned; Pu disagreed, and both views were submitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, after the heir's investiture rites, the Grand Secretariat debated an amnesty. Manchu ministers argued that fugitive bannermen should be excluded; Pu objected, and both positions were forwarded to the throne.

sentences.zh: 詔下閣臣畫一奏聞，有謂當從滿大臣議者，溥持之力，仍以兩議進，上卒從之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the grand secretaries to settle on one view and report. Some said the Manchu ministers' view should be followed; Pu maintained his position with force, still submitting both views—and the emperor ultimately concurred with him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the Grand Secretariat to reach a unified recommendation. Some advised following the Manchu ministers; Pu held firm and again submitted both proposals. In the end the emperor sided with Pu.

sentences.zh: 十七年，福建平，溥以年屆七十，復申前請，上仍慰留。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, Fujian was pacified. Pu, having reached seventy years of age, renewed his earlier request; the emperor again urged him to stay.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, after Fujian was pacified, Pu petitioned once more, now that he had turned seventy; the emperor again declined to release him.

sentences.zh: 二十一年秋，詔許致仕，遣官護行馳驛如故事。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the twenty-first year, an edict permitted him to retire. Officials were dispatched to escort him home by express courier post, according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of his twenty-first year in office, he was granted permission to retire, with officials sent to escort him home by relay post as customary.

sentences.zh: 比將歸，詣闕謝，賜遊西苑，內侍攜酒果，所至坐飲三爵。

translations.literal: As he was about to depart, he went to the palace to give thanks. He was granted a tour of the Western Park; eunuchs carried wine and fruit, and wherever he stopped he was seated and offered three cups.
translations.idiomatic: Before leaving, he went to court to bid farewell. The emperor granted him a stroll through the Western Park, with eunuchs bearing wine and fruit; at each stop he was seated and served three rounds of drink.

sentences.zh: 臨發，疏請清心省事，與民休息，言甚切，溫旨報聞。

translations.literal: On the eve of departure, he memorialized urging the emperor to simplify affairs of state and let the people rest; his words were earnest, and a warm edict acknowledged them.
translations.idiomatic: Just before setting out, he submitted a memorial pleading for leaner government and relief for the people—worded with great urgency—and received a gracious reply in edict form.

sentences.zh: 賜御製詩及「適志東山」篆章，命講官牛鈕、陳廷敬傳諭曰：「朕聞山東仕於朝者，彼此援引，造為議論，務有濟於私，又居鄉多擾害地方，朕審知其弊。

translations.literal: He was granted an imperial poem and a seal engraved with "Contented Ambition in the Eastern Hills." Lecturers Niu Niu and Chen Tingjing were ordered to relay the message: "I have heard that Shandong officials serving at court recommend one another and spin arguments to serve private ends, and that many who live in their home districts disturb and harm the locality—I am well aware of these abuses.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor bestowed an imperial poem and a seal bearing the characters "Contentment on the Eastern Hills," and dispatched lecturers Niu Niu and Chen Tingjing to convey his words: "I have heard that Shandong men in office at court band together, promote one another, and manufacture disputes to advance private interest, while those who return home often bring trouble to their districts. I know this well.

sentences.zh: 馮溥久居禁密，可教訓子孫，務為安靜。」

translations.literal: Feng Pu has long served in the inner precincts—he can instruct his descendants to keep quiet and restrained."
translations.idiomatic: Feng Pu has served long within the palace inner circle; let him teach his descendants to conduct themselves with restraint and decorum."

sentences.zh: 太宗實錄成，加太子太傅。

translations.literal: When the Veritable Records of Taizong were completed, he was made Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Upon completion of the Veritable Records of Taizong, he was promoted to Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 三十年，卒，年八十三，諡文毅。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, he died at the age of eighty-three, posthumously titled Wenyi.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year he died, aged eighty-three, and was given the posthumous name Wenyi.

sentences.zh: 溥居京師，闢万柳堂，與諸名士觴詠其中。

translations.literal: While living in the capital, Pu opened the Wanliu Hall and drank and composed verse there with eminent literati.
translations.idiomatic: During his residence in the capital, Pu established the Wanliu Hall, where he shared wine and poetry with leading men of letters.

sentences.zh: 性愛才，聞賢能，輒大書姓名於座隅，備薦擢。

translations.literal: By nature he loved talent; whenever he heard of someone able and worthy, he would write the name in large characters in a corner of his seat, preparing to recommend and promote them.
translations.idiomatic: He had a passion for talent; upon hearing of anyone capable and worthy, he would jot their name in bold characters nearby, keeping them in mind for recommendation.

sentences.zh: 一時士論歸之。

translations.literal: For a time, scholarly opinion looked to him.
translations.idiomatic: For a time, public opinion among the educated class rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 王熙，字子雍，順天宛平人。

translations.literal: Wang Xi, courtesy name Ziyong, was a native of Wanping in Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xi, styled Ziyong, came from Wanping in Shuntian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父崇簡，明崇禎十六年進士。

translations.literal: His father Chongjian passed the jinshi examination in the sixteenth year of the Chongzhen reign of the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: His father, Chongjian, earned his jinshi degree in the sixteenth year of Ming Chongzhen.

sentences.zh: 順治三年，以順天學政曹溶薦，補選庶吉士，授檢討。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shunzhi, on recommendation of Cao Rong, educational commissioner of Shuntian, he was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy and appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 3, recommended by Shuntian educational commissioner Cao Rong, he entered the Hanlin as a probationary bachelor and was made a reviser.

sentences.zh: 累遷禮部尚書，加太子少保。

translations.literal: He was progressively promoted to Minister of Rites and given the additional title of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive appointments to Minister of Rites, with the additional rank of Junior Guardian of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 嘗疏請賜血卩明季殉難範景文、蔡懋德等二十八人，又議帝王廟罷宋臣潘美、張浚從祀，北岳移祀渾源，皆用其議。

translations.literal: He once memorialized requesting posthumous honors for twenty-eight Ming loyalists who died in the cause, including Fan Jingwen and Cai Maode; he also proposed removing Song ministers Pan Mei and Zhang Jun from the Imperial Temple, and relocating the Northern Peak shrine to Hunyuan—all were adopted.
translations.idiomatic: He once petitioned for posthumous ennoblement of twenty-eight martyrs of the late Ming, among them Fan Jingwen and Cai Maode. He also recommended removing the Song ministers Pan Mei and Zhang Jun from the Imperial Ancestral Temple and moving worship of the Northern Peak to Hunyuan—all proposals were accepted.

sentences.zh: 十八年，引疾解職。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, citing illness, he resigned his office.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he retired from office, pleading illness.

sentences.zh: 康熙十七年，卒，諡文貞。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Kangxi, he died and was posthumously titled Wenzhen.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Kangxi 17 and received the posthumous name Wenzhen.

sentences.zh: 熙，順治四年進士，選庶吉士，授檢討。

translations.literal: Xi passed the jinshi examination in the fourth year of Shunzhi, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xi himself took his jinshi in Shunzhi 4, entered the Hanlin, and was appointed reviser.

sentences.zh: 累遷右春坊諭德。

translations.literal: He was progressively promoted to Preceptor of the Right Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to Preceptor in the Right Secretariat of the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 召直南苑。

translations.literal: He was summoned to serve on duty at the Southern Park.
translations.idiomatic: He was called to attend the emperor at the Southern Imperial Park.

sentences.zh: 譯大學衍義，充日講官，進講稱旨。

translations.literal: He translated the Extension of the Great Learning, served as daily lecturer, and his lecturing pleased the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: He translated the Daxue Yanyi, served as a daily lecturer at court, and his expositions met with imperial approval.

sentences.zh: 累擢弘文院學士。

translations.literal: He was progressively promoted to Academician of the Hall of Literary Glory.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to become an Academician of the Hall of Literary Glory.

sentences.zh: 時崇簡方任國史院學士，上曰：「父子同官，古今所罕。

translations.literal: At that time Chongjian was serving as Academician of the Historiography Institute. The emperor said: "Father and son holding office together is rare in all ages.
translations.idiomatic: Chongjian was then serving as an Academician of the Historiography Institute. The emperor remarked: "For father and son to hold office simultaneously is scarcely seen in history.

sentences.zh: 以爾誠恪，特加此恩。」

translations.literal: Because of your sincerity and dutifulness, this special favor is granted."
translations.idiomatic: In recognition of your loyalty and integrity, I confer this exceptional honor."

sentences.zh: 十五年，擢禮部侍郎，兼翰林院掌院學士。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, he was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites and concurrently made Chief Academician of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was elevated to Vice Minister of Rites and concurrently appointed Chief Academician of the Hanlin.

sentences.zh: 考滿，加尚書銜。

translations.literal: Upon completion of his tenure assessment, he was given the titular rank of minister.
translations.idiomatic: After his performance review, he received the honorary rank of minister.

sentences.zh: 時崇簡為尚書，父子復同官。
