translations.literal: At that time Chongjian was minister, and father and son again held office together.
translations.idiomatic: By then Chongjian had become a full minister, and father and son once again served side by side.

sentences.zh: 十八年正月，上大漸，召熙至養心殿撰遺詔，熙伏地飲泣，筆不能下，上諭勉抑哀痛，即禦榻前先草第一條以進。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eighteenth year, the emperor's illness worsened. Wang Xi was summoned to the Hall of Mental Cultivation to draft the deathbed edict. Wang Xi prostrated himself weeping and could not bring pen to paper. The emperor urged him to restrain his grief and, right before the imperial couch, personally drafted the first article and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the eighteenth year, as the emperor lay gravely ill, Wang Xi was summoned to the Hall of Mental Cultivation to compose the testament. Wang Xi fell prostrate, weeping so hard he could not write. The emperor bade him master his grief and, from his sickbed, personally drafted the first clause for him to submit.

sentences.zh: 尋奏移乾清門撰擬，進呈者三，皆報可。

translations.literal: Soon thereafter it was reported that drafting was moved to the Gate of Heavenly Purity; three drafts were submitted, all approved.
translations.idiomatic: Work then shifted to the Gate of Heavenly Purity; three versions were submitted, each approved.

sentences.zh: 是夕上崩，聖祖嗣位，熙改兼弘文院學士。

translations.literal: That evening the emperor died. The Sacred Ancestor succeeded to the throne, and Wang Xi was reassigned to serve concurrently as Academician of the Hall of Literary Glory.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor passed away that night. When the Kangxi Emperor ascended the throne, Wang Xi was retained as Academician of the Hall of Literary Glory.

sentences.zh: 康熙五年，遷左都御史。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Kangxi, he was transferred to Censor-in-Chief of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 5 he was appointed Censor-in-Chief of the Left.

sentences.zh: 時三籓擁兵踰制，吳三桂尤崛強，擅署官吏，浸驕蹇，萌異志。

translations.literal: At that time the Three Feudatories held armies beyond their authorized strength; Wu Sangui was especially overbearing, appointing officials on his own authority, growing arrogant and defiant, and harboring rebellious intentions.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Feudatories had exceeded their military allotments; Wu Sangui in particular had grown defiant, appointing officials at will, waxing ever more insolent until disloyal ambitions took shape.

sentences.zh: 子應熊，以尚主居京師，多聚奸人，散金錢，交通四方。

translations.literal: His son Yingxiong, having married an imperial princess and residing in the capital, gathered many villainous men, disbursed money, and maintained contacts in all directions.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui's son Yingxiong, who lived in the capital as consort to an imperial princess, assembled ruffians, spent freely, and maintained networks across the empire.

sentences.zh: 熙首疏請裁兵減餉，略言：「直省錢糧，半為雲、貴、湖廣兵餉所耗。

translations.literal: Wang Xi was the first to memorialize requesting troop cuts and ration reductions, stating in summary: "Half the revenue of the directly administered provinces is consumed by military pay for Yunnan, Guizhou, Huguang, and related areas.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xi took the lead in petitioning for force reductions and pay cuts, writing in part: "Fully half the grain revenue of the provinces goes to sustaining troops in Yunnan, Guizhou, and Huguang.

sentences.zh: 就雲、貴言，籓下官兵歲需俸餉三百餘萬，本省賦稅不足供什一，勢難經久。

translations.literal: Taking Yunnan and Guizhou alone, the feudatory's officers and troops require over three million taels in annual pay and provisions; the provinces' land tax yields less than a tenth of that—it cannot long be sustained.
translations.idiomatic: In Yunnan and Guizhou alone, the feudatory's forces draw over three million taels yearly in pay and rations, while local tax revenue covers less than a tenth—a situation that cannot endure.

sentences.zh: 臣以為滇、黔已平，綠旗額兵亟宜汰減，即籓下餘丁，亦宜散遣屯種，則勢分而餉亦裕。」

translations.literal: Your subject holds that since Yunnan and Guizhou are pacified, the authorized Green Banner troops should urgently be reduced. Even the feudatory's remaining men should be dispersed for garrison farming—thus dividing their strength and easing the burden on pay."
translations.idiomatic: I believe that with Dian and Qian pacified, the Green Banner quotas should be cut at once, and the feudatory's surplus manpower dispersed to farming colonies—splitting their power while stretching the pay budget further."

sentences.zh: 复疏言：「閩、廣、江西、湖廣等省官吏，挾貲貿易，與民爭利。

translations.literal: He further memorialized: "In Fujian, Guangdong, Jiangxi, Huguang, and other provinces, officials trade with their capital and compete with the people for profit.
translations.idiomatic: In a follow-up memorial he wrote: "Officials in Fujian, Guangdong, Jiangxi, Huguang, and elsewhere engage in trade on the side, competing with commoners for profit.

sentences.zh: 或指稱籓下，依勢橫行。

translations.literal: Some claim affiliation with the feudatory and act with impunity by its power.
translations.idiomatic: Some invoke the feudatory's name and throw their weight around accordingly.

sentences.zh: 宜飭嚴禁。」

translations.literal: Strict prohibition should be ordered."
translations.idiomatic: Strict enforcement is called for."

sentences.zh: 又言：「近例招民百家送至盛京，得授知縣。

translations.literal: He also said: "Under a recent regulation, anyone who recruits a hundred households and escorts them to Mukden may be appointed county magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: He added: "A recent rule allows appointment as county magistrate to anyone who brings a hundred households to Mukden.

sentences.zh: 不肖奸人，借資為市，貽害地方，宜改給散秩。

translations.literal: Unworthy scoundrels use borrowed capital to trade in this privilege, harming the locality—it should be changed to awarding only honorary rank without substantive appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Unscrupulous men buy their way in, harming local communities; the reward should be reduced to an honorary title only.

sentences.zh: 現任官吏捐輸銀米，博取議敘，名出私橐，實取諸民，宜一切報罷。」

translations.literal: Incumbent officials donate silver and grain to win favorable performance reviews—nominally from private purses, in fact extracted from the people. All such practices should be abolished."
translations.idiomatic: Serving officials who donate silver and grain to earn merit citations claim private expense but actually squeeze the people—all such schemes should be cancelled."

sentences.zh: 上俱從之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved all of these.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted every proposal.

sentences.zh: 七年夏，旱，金星晝見，詔求直言。

translations.literal: In the summer of the seventh year, drought prevailed and Venus appeared by day; an edict sought forthright criticism.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the seventh year, drought afflicted the land and Venus was visible in daylight; the throne issued a call for candid counsel.

sentences.zh: 熙疏言：「世祖章皇帝精勤圖治，諸曹政務，皆經詳定。

translations.literal: Wang Xi memorialized: "The Shizu Zhang Emperor applied himself diligently to governance; the affairs of every department were carefully settled.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xi submitted a memorial: "The Shizu Emperor devoted himself tirelessly to governing; every branch of administration had been carefully regulated under his hand.

sentences.zh: 數年來有因言官條奏改易者，有因各部院題請更張者，有會議興革者，則例繁多，官吏奉行，任意輕重。

translations.literal: In recent years, some changes came through censorial memorials, some through requests from ministries and courts, some through conference-driven reforms—so precedents multiplied, and officials in carrying them out applied them arbitrarily, with varying severity.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years changes have been driven by censorial memorials, by petitions from individual ministries, and by conference resolutions—with the result that regulations have proliferated and officials enforce them as they please, inconsistently.

sentences.zh: 請敕部院諸司詳察現行事例，有因變法而滋弊者，悉遵舊制更正。

translations.literal: I request that ministries, courts, and their bureaus be ordered to examine current precedents in detail; where change of law has bred abuse, all should be corrected by reverting to the old system.
translations.idiomatic: I urge that every ministry and bureau scrutinize existing regulations and restore the former system wherever reforms have introduced abuse.

sentences.zh: 其有從新例便者，亦條晰不得不然之故，裁定畫一。」

translations.literal: Where the new precedent is genuinely advantageous, the reasons why it must be so should also be set forth item by item, and a uniform ruling made."
translations.idiomatic: Where newer rules truly serve better, let the reasons be spelled out clearly case by case, and let a single standard be fixed for all."

sentences.zh: 上命各部院條議，遵舊制，刪繁例​​，凡數十事。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered each ministry and court to submit detailed proposals, reverting to old systems and pruning redundant precedents—altogether several dozen matters.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor directed the ministries to deliberate item by item, restore older practices, and cut redundant regulations—addressing several dozen items in all.

sentences.zh: 遷工部尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 十二年，調兵部。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, he was transferred to the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he moved to the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，三桂反，京師聞變，都城內外一夕火四起，皆應熊黨為之也。

translations.literal: That winter Wu Sangui rebelled. When word reached the capital, fires broke out on all sides within and without the city in a single night—all the work of Yingxiong's faction.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, when Wu Sangui rebelled and news reached the capital, fires erupted across the city in a single night—all set by partisans of Yingxiong.

sentences.zh: 明年三月，用熙言誅應熊。

translations.literal: The following March, on Wang Xi's advice, Yingxiong was executed.
translations.idiomatic: The following March, acting on Wang Xi's counsel, Yingxiong was put to death.

sentences.zh: 尋命熙專管密本。

translations.literal: Soon Wang Xi was ordered to take sole charge of confidential memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xi was soon put in exclusive charge of classified memorials.

sentences.zh: 漢臣與聞軍機自熙始。

translations.literal: Han officials' participation in military planning began with Wang Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Han ministers first gained access to military deliberations through Wang Xi.

sentences.zh: 十七年，以父憂去。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, he left office due to mourning for his father.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he resigned to observe mourning for his father.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，即家拜保和殿大學士，兼禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, while still at home, he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Hall of Preserving Harmony and concurrently Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Hall of Preserving Harmony and Minister of Rites without leaving home.

sentences.zh: 時三籓既平，熙以和平寬大，宣上德意，與民休息。

translations.literal: The Three Feudatories had just been pacified. Wang Xi, with mild and generous bearing, proclaimed the emperor's benevolent intent and sought repose for the people.
translations.idiomatic: With the Three Feudatories recently subdued, Wang Xi communicated the emperor's clemency in measured, generous terms and pressed for policies that would let the people recover.

sentences.zh: 造次奏對，直陳無隱，上每傾聽。

translations.literal: In urgent audiences he spoke plainly without concealment, and the emperor always listened with full attention.
translations.idiomatic: Even in hasty audiences he spoke without reserve, and the emperor always gave him a hearing.

sentences.zh: 太祖實錄成，加太子太傅。

translations.literal: When the Veritable Records of Taizu were completed, he was made Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Upon completion of the Veritable Records of Taizu, he was promoted to Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，以疾累疏乞休，溫旨慰留。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year, citing illness, he repeatedly memorialized to retire; warm edicts urged him to remain.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year he repeatedly asked to retire on grounds of illness, but gracious edicts kept him in office.

sentences.zh: 四十年，詔許致仕，晉少傅。

translations.literal: In the fortieth year, an edict permitted retirement, and he was promoted to Junior Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fortieth year he was granted permission to retire and promoted to Junior Tutor.

sentences.zh: 明年上元節，賜宴其家，遣官齎手敕存問。

translations.literal: The following year on the Lantern Festival, a banquet was granted at his home, and officials were dispatched bearing an imperial autograph letter of inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: On the Lantern Festival the following year, the emperor hosted a feast at his residence and sent officials with a personal letter of regard.

sentences.zh: 四十二年，卒，上命皇長子直郡王允禔、大學士馬齊臨喪，行拜奠禮，舉哀酹酒，恩禮有加，諡文靖。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year he died. The emperor ordered the eldest imperial son, Prince of the First Rank Yunzhi, and Grand Secretary Ma Qi to attend the funeral, perform obeisance and offering rites, raise lamentation and pour libation wine—honors beyond the usual—and he was posthumously titled Wenjing.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the forty-second year. The Kangxi Emperor sent his eldest son, Prince Yunzhi, and Grand Secretary Ma Qi to the funeral with orders to perform obeisance, offer libations, and mourn on the throne's behalf—honors rarely accorded—and conferred the posthumous name Wenjing.

sentences.zh: 熙持大體，有遠慮。

translations.literal: Wang Xi grasped the larger principles and possessed far-sighted forethought.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xi kept sight of the larger picture and thought far ahead.

sentences.zh: 平定三籓後，開方略館。

translations.literal: After the Three Feudatories were pacified, the Strategy Office was opened.
translations.idiomatic: After the pacification of the Three Feudatories, the Strategy Office was established.

sentences.zh: 一日，上諭閣臣：「當三桂反時，漢官有言不必發兵，七旬有苗格者。」

translations.literal: One day the emperor instructed the grand secretaries: "When Wu Sangui rebelled, some Han officials said troops need not be dispatched—that at seventy days the Miao would submit."
translations.idiomatic: One day the emperor told the Grand Secretariat: "When Wu Sangui rebelled, some Han officials argued against sending troops, saying the Miao would surrender within seventy days."

sentences.zh: 又其時漢官多移妻子回家，顧學士韓菼曰：「汝為朕載之！」

translations.literal: He also said that at that time many Han officials sent wives and children home. Turning to Academician Han Tan, he said: "You shall record this for Me!"
translations.idiomatic: He noted that many Han officials had meanwhile sent their families home. Addressing Academician Han Tan, he said: "Record this for me!"

sentences.zh: 菼退而皇恐。

translations.literal: Han Tan withdrew in dread.
translations.idiomatic: Han Tan withdrew in terror.

sentences.zh: 熙乃昌言閣中曰：「『有苗格『乃會議時魏象樞語。

translations.literal: Wang Xi then spoke forthrightly in the Grand Secretariat: "The phrase 'the Miao will submit' was Wei Xiangsu's words during the conference deliberations.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xi then spoke boldly within the Grand Secretariat: "The remark about 'the Miao submitting' came from Wei Xiangsu during the deliberations.

sentences.zh: 告者截去首尾，遂失其本意。

translations.literal: The informant cut away the beginning and end, thus losing the original intent.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever reported it stripped away the context, distorting the original meaning.

sentences.zh: 然如其言，豈非誤國？

translations.literal: Yet if taken as he said, would that not have been a disaster for the state?
translations.idiomatic: Even so, had we acted on those words alone, would that not have been national calamity?

sentences.zh: 移家偶然耳，日久何從分別，其移者豈非背主？

translations.literal: Moving one's family home was a matter of chance—over time how could one distinguish? Are those who moved not disloyal to their lord?
translations.idiomatic: Sending one's family home might happen for any number of reasons—given time, who could tell them apart? And are those who did so not guilty of deserting their sovereign?

sentences.zh: 漢官負此兩大罪，何顏立朝？」

translations.literal: Han officials bearing these two great crimes—what face have they to stand at court?"
translations.idiomatic: With these two grave charges hanging over Han officials, how could any of them hold up their heads at court?"

sentences.zh: 翌日入見，執奏如閣中語，上許之。

translations.literal: The next day, entering audience, he submitted as he had spoken in the Grand Secretariat, and the emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he repeated these arguments to the emperor in audience, and his account was accepted.

sentences.zh: 熙子克善、克勤，皆世祖命名。

translations.literal: Wang Xi's sons Keshan and Keqin were both named by the Shizu Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xi's sons Keshan and Keqin both received their names from the Shizu Emperor.

sentences.zh: 克善能文，熙不令與試，遇鄉、會典試，熙輒注假，以聖祖方惡漢人師生之習，故尤慎之。

translations.literal: Keshan was skilled in letters, but Wang Xi would not let him sit for examinations. Whenever provincial or metropolitan exams were held, Wang Xi would note leave for him, because the Sacred Ancestor then disapproved of teacher-student networking among Han Chinese—and Wang Xi was especially cautious.
translations.idiomatic: Though Keshan was a gifted writer, Wang Xi forbade him from taking the exams; at every provincial or metropolitan session he would record sick leave on his son's behalf, for the Kangxi Emperor then looked unfavorably on patronage networks among Han literati, and Wang Xi was doubly careful.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，典會試，蓋特命也。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he presided over the metropolitan examination—a special appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year he was specially appointed chief examiner for the metropolitan exams.

sentences.zh: 雍正中。

translations.literal: During the Yongzheng reign.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Yongzheng Emperor.

sentences.zh: 入祀賢良祠。

translations.literal: He was enshrined in the Temple of Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He was admitted to the Temple of Worthies.

sentences.zh: 弟燕，字子喜，以父廕，任戶部郎中。

translations.literal: His younger brother Yan, courtesy name Zixi, through his father's privilege of office, served as Director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Yan, styled Zixi, entered office through his father's yin privilege and served as a Director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 出為鎮江知府，擢江蘇按察使，治獄稱平。

translations.literal: He went out as prefect of Zhenjiang, was promoted to judicial commissioner of Jiangsu, and his handling of cases was reckoned fair.
translations.idiomatic: Posted as prefect of Zhenjiang, he rose to Jiangsu judicial commissioner, earning repute for even-handed justice.

sentences.zh: 遷湖廣布政使，巡撫貴州，建學設官，減賦稅，教養兼施，善拊循苗人，頒條教，飭州縣無縱奸人詭索土司。

translations.literal: He was transferred to financial commissioner of Huguang and served as governor of Guizhou. He established schools and appointed officials, reduced taxes and levies, combining instruction with nurture. He was skilled at comforting the Miao people, issued regulations, and ordered prefectures and counties not to allow scoundrels to extort under false pretenses from native chieftains.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Huguang financial commissioner and appointed governor of Guizhou, he founded schools, reduced taxes, and pursued both education and welfare. He won over the Miao with gentle governance, issued regulations, and forbade local officials from letting scoundrels fleece native chieftains through fraudulent demands.

sentences.zh: 撫黔三年，移疾歸，卒。

translations.literal: After three years governing Guizhou, he cited illness and returned home, then died.
translations.idiomatic: After three years in Guizhou he retired citing illness and died shortly after returning home.

sentences.zh: 吳正治，字當世，湖北江夏人。

translations.literal: Wu Zhengzhi, courtesy name Dangshi, was a native of Jiangxia in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zhengzhi, styled Dangshi, came from Jiangxia in Hubei.

sentences.zh: 順治六年進士，選庶吉士，授國史院編修。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the sixth year of Shunzhi, he was selected as Hanlin bachelor and appointed compiler in the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi in Shunzhi 6, entered the Hanlin, and was appointed compiler of the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，服闋，起故官。

translations.literal: Upon completing mourning for his mother, he resumed his former office.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his mother, he returned to his previous post.

sentences.zh: 遷右庶子。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 十五年，特簡翰林官十五人外用，正治與焉，得江西南昌道。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, fifteen Hanlin officials were specially selected for provincial posts; Zhengzhi was among them and received the Jiangxi Nanchang circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year, fifteen Hanlin academicians were specially chosen for provincial service; Zhengzhi was selected and appointed to the Nanchang circuit in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 遷陝西按察使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to judicial commissioner of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to judicial commissioner of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 所至以清廉執法著稱。

translations.literal: Every place he arrived at, he was famed for integrity and strict law enforcement.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served, he won renown for integrity and impartial enforcement of the law.

sentences.zh: 十七年，內擢工部侍郎，調刑部。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, he was promoted from within to Vice President of the Ministry of Works and transferred to the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was elevated from within the court to Vice President of Works, then transferred to Punishments.

sentences.zh: 平亭疑獄，釋江南逋賦無辜諸生二百餘人。

translations.literal: He evenly settled doubtful criminal cases and released more than two hundred innocent student scholars from Jiangnan implicated in tax arrears.
translations.idiomatic: He adjudicated doubtful cases with evenhanded justice and freed more than two hundred innocent Jiangnan scholars wrongly caught up in tax-arrears prosecutions.

sentences.zh: 疏論奉行赦款宜速，丈量田地宜停，禁狀外指扳，嚴婦女私嫁，皆著為令。

translations.literal: In a memorial he argued that implementing amnesty provisions should be expedited, land surveying should be halted, indictments beyond the complaint should be forbidden, and clandestine marriages of women should be strictly prohibited—all were promulgated as regulations.
translations.idiomatic: In memorials he urged swift implementation of amnesty clauses, a halt to land surveys, a ban on implicating people not named in the original complaint, and strict prohibition of unauthorized marriages among women; all were enacted as law.

sentences.zh: 康熙八年，以父憂去。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Kangxi, he left office on account of mourning for his father.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 8 he resigned to observe mourning for his father.

sentences.zh: 起兵部督捕侍郎，充經筵講官。

translations.literal: He rose to Vice President of the Ministry of War in charge of apprehending fugitives and served as lecturer at the classics colloquium.
translations.idiomatic: Upon returning to office he was appointed Vice President of War for fugitive apprehension and lectured at the imperial classics colloquium.

sentences.zh: 十二年，遷左都御史。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, he was transferred to Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「緝逃事例，首嚴窩隱。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "In the regulations on apprehending fugitives, harboring is punished most severely.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial: "Under the fugitive-apprehension regulations, harboring is treated as the gravest offense.

sentences.zh: 一有容留，雖親如父子，即坐以罪，使小民父子視若仇讎。

translations.literal: Once anyone is given shelter, even if as close as father and son, guilt is immediately imputed, causing common people to regard father and son as if they were enemies.
translations.idiomatic: The moment anyone gives shelter—even to a kinsman as close as father and son—guilt follows at once, until common folk look upon their own fathers and sons as enemies.

sentences.zh: 伏讀律有親屬容隱之條，惟叛逆者不用此律。

translations.literal: Bowing and reading the code, there is a provision on harboring by relatives; only rebels are not subject to this law.
translations.idiomatic: On reverent study of the code, one finds a statute permitting relatives to harbor one another—yet rebels alone are excluded from its protection.

sentences.zh: 逃人乃旗下家人之事，與​​叛逆輕重相懸。

translations.literal: Fugitive slaves are a matter of banner household retainers; the gravity of the offense is vastly different from rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Runaway banner bondservants are a domestic household matter, far removed in gravity from treason.

sentences.zh: 請自今有父子窩逃，被人舉發者，逃犯治罪，免坐窩隱。

translations.literal: I request that from now on, when father and son harbor a fugitive and are reported by others, the fugitive be punished but harboring guilt be waived.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that hereafter, when father and son are found to have sheltered a fugitive and are denounced by others, only the fugitive be punished and the harboring charge be set aside.

sentences.zh: 若容留逾旬，父子首報者，逃犯依自首例減罪。

translations.literal: If shelter lasts more than ten days and father and son report first, the fugitive's penalty shall be reduced according to the rule on voluntary surrender.
translations.idiomatic: If the fugitive has been hidden for more than ten days and the father and son come forward first, the runaway's sentence should be reduced as for voluntary surrender.

sentences.zh: 則首報者多，逃人易獲。

translations.literal: Then there will be many first reports, and fugitives will be easy to capture.
translations.idiomatic: More people would come forward to report, and fugitives would be easier to apprehend.

sentences.zh: 朝廷之法與天性之恩，兩不相悖矣。」

translations.literal: The court's law and natural filial affection would not contradict each other."
translations.idiomatic: The law of the court and the claims of natural affection would no longer stand at odds."

sentences.zh: 又言：「今歲雨澤愆期，方事祈禱。

translations.literal: He also said: "This year rain has failed to arrive on schedule; we are presently engaged in prayer for rain.
translations.idiomatic: He went on: "This year the rains are overdue, and the court is already at prayer for them.

sentences.zh: 近因直隸多盜，廷議於玉田、灤州、霸州、雄縣增設駐防旗兵，構建營房，勞民動眾，應暫停止。

translations.literal: Recently, because Zhili has many bandits, the court deliberated adding garrison banner troops at Yutian, Luanzhou, Bazhou, and Xiong County and constructing barracks—burdening the people and mobilizing the masses—this should temporarily be halted.
translations.idiomatic: Recently, with banditry rife in Zhili, the court had debated posting additional garrison banner troops at Yutian, Luanzhou, Bazhou, and Xiong County and building barracks—a laborious undertaking that should be suspended for the present.

sentences.zh: 俟農隙時酌行。」

translations.literal: Wait until the agricultural slack season to implement as appropriate."
translations.idiomatic: It should be carried out later, when the farming season allows."

sentences.zh: 疏入，下部議，俱如所請。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, it was referred to the ministries for deliberation, and all requests were granted.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was received, referred to the ministries, and approved in full.

sentences.zh: 先是睿親王多爾袞當國，嚴旗下逃人之禁，鰲拜繼之，禁益嚴。

translations.literal: Previously, when Prince Rui Dorgon held power, he strictly enforced the ban on banner fugitives; Oboi continued this policy, and the prohibition grew ever harsher.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Prince Rui Dorgon governed the realm, he had imposed a harsh ban on runaway banner bondservants; Oboi carried the policy forward and tightened it still further.

sentences.zh: 株連窮治，天下囂然，而圈地建營房，凡涉旗務，漢大臣莫敢置喙。

translations.literal: Implicating neighbors in relentless prosecutions, the realm was in uproar; yet regarding land appropriation and barrack construction, whenever banner affairs were involved, Han grand ministers dared not utter a word.
translations.idiomatic: Relentless prosecutions that dragged in the innocent threw the empire into an uproar, yet on land seizures, barrack construction, and every matter touching the banners, Han ministers did not dare speak.

sentences.zh: 自正治疏出，逃人禁稍寬，營房亦罷建，世多以是稱之。

translations.literal: Since Zhengzhi's memorial appeared, the fugitive ban was slightly relaxed and barrack construction was halted; the age largely praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhengzhi's memorial, the fugitive laws were eased somewhat and barrack construction was abandoned; contemporaries widely praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 尋遷工部尚書，調禮部。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Minister of Works and then to the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Minister of Works and then transferred to Rites.

sentences.zh: 十八年，自陳乞休，詔嘉其端勤誠慎，慰留之。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, he petitioned to retire; an edict praised his uprightness, diligence, sincerity, and prudence and urged him to remain.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he asked to retire; the throne commended his integrity, diligence, sincerity, and caution, and pressed him to stay on.

sentences.zh: 二十年，拜武英殿大學士。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Hall of Martial Eminence.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he was made Grand Secretary of the Hall of Martial Eminence.

sentences.zh: 時修太祖實錄、聖訓、會典、方略、一統志，俱充總裁官，加太子太傅。

translations.literal: At the time the Taizu Veritable Records, Sacred Instructions, Collected Statutes, Military Annals, and Unified Gazetteer were being compiled; he served as chief editor for all of them and was promoted to Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: While the Veritable Records of Taizu, the Sacred Instructions, the Collected Statutes, the Military Annals, and the Unified Gazetteer were under compilation, he served as chief editor of them all and was given the rank of Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 正治守成法，識大體。

translations.literal: Zhengzhi upheld established law and grasped the larger pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengzhi adhered to established precedent and understood the larger stakes.

sentences.zh: 一日，聖祖閱朝審冊，有以刃刺人股致死而抵法者，上曰：「刺股傷非致命，此可寬也。」

translations.literal: One day the Sage Ancestor reviewed the capital-case dossiers. There was a man who had stabbed another's thigh with a blade, causing death, and faced punishment. The Emperor said: "A thigh wound is not necessarily fatal; this may be treated leniently."
translations.idiomatic: One day the Emperor reviewed capital-case records and came upon a man condemned for stabbing another in the thigh with a blade and causing death. The Emperor said, "A thigh wound is not necessarily mortal; this sentence may be eased."

sentences.zh: 正治對曰：「當念死者之無辜。」

translations.literal: Zhengzhi replied: "One must consider the dead man's innocence."
translations.idiomatic: Zhengzhi answered, "Your Majesty should also remember that the dead man was innocent of any wrong."

sentences.zh: 他日，又閱冊，有囚當死，上問此囚尚可活否，眾皆以情實對。

translations.literal: On another day, reviewing the dossiers again, there was a prisoner who deserved death. The Emperor asked whether this prisoner could still live; everyone answered according to the facts of the case.
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion, while reviewing cases, he found a prisoner sentenced to death and asked whether the man might be spared. The others all answered according to the facts.

sentences.zh: 正治曰：「皇上好生之德，臣等敢不奉行。」

translations.literal: Zhengzhi said: "Your Majesty's virtue of cherishing life—how dare we ministers not carry it out?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhengzhi said, "Your Majesty's mercy toward life is well known—how could we ministers fail to honor it?"

sentences.zh: 退而細勘，得可矜狀，遂從末減。

translations.literal: After withdrawing, he examined the case closely, found mitigating circumstances, and then applied the lowest degree of reduction.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he reviewed the case in detail, found grounds for clemency, and had the sentence reduced to the lowest permissible degree.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，复疏乞休，詔許原官致仕。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, he again memorialized to retire; an edict permitted him to retire at his original rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he again asked to retire, and the throne allowed him to leave office at his existing rank.

sentences.zh: 三十年，卒，諡文僖。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he died; his posthumous title was Wenxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year he died and was posthumously titled Wenxi.

sentences.zh: 黃機，字次辰，浙江錢塘人。

translations.literal: Huang Ji, courtesy name Cichen, was a native of Qiantang in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Ji, styled Cichen, came from Qiantang in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 順治四年進士，選庶吉士，授弘文院編修。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the fourth year of Shunzhi, he was selected as Hanlin bachelor and appointed compiler in the Hongwen Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi in Shunzhi 4, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and was appointed compiler of the Hongwen Academy.

sentences.zh: 世祖幸內院，詢機裡籍官職，命與侍講法若真、修撰呂宮、編修程芳朝撰柳下惠不以三公易其介論，上覽畢，賜茶。

translations.literal: The Shizu Emperor visited the Inner Academy, inquired into Ji's native place and official posts, and ordered him, together with Lecturer Fa Ruozhen, Compiler Lü Gong, and Compiler Cheng Fangchao, to compose "On How Liu Xiahui Would Not Exchange His Integrity for the Three Ducal Titles." When the Emperor had finished reading it, he bestowed tea.
translations.idiomatic: When the Shizu Emperor visited the Inner Academy, he asked after Ji's birthplace and office and ordered him, with Lecturer Fa Ruozhen, Compiler Lü Gong, and Compiler Cheng Fangchao, to write an essay on Liu Xiahui's refusal to trade his integrity for high office. The Emperor read it through and rewarded them with tea.

sentences.zh: 授左中允，尋遷弘文院侍讀。

translations.literal: He was appointed Left Sub-Reader and soon transferred to Reader in the Hongwen Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Left Sub-Reader and soon promoted to Reader of the Hongwen Academy.

sentences.zh: 十二年，機疏言：「自古仁聖之君，必祖述前謨，以昭一代文明之治。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, Ji memorialized: "Since antiquity, benevolent and sage rulers have always traced and followed the counsels of their predecessors to display one generation's civilized governance.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year Ji submitted a memorial: "From antiquity, benevolent and sage rulers have looked back to the counsels of earlier ages to make their own civil rule shine forth.

sentences.zh: 今纂修太祖、太宗實錄告成，乞敕諸臣校定所載嘉言嘉行，仿貞觀政要、洪武寶訓諸書，輯成治典，頒行天下。

translations.literal: Now that compilation of the Taizu and Taizong Veritable Records is complete, I beg that ministers be ordered to collate the fine words and fine deeds recorded therein, model the work after books such as Essentials of Governance from the Zhenguan Reign and Sacred Instructions of the Hongwu Reign, compile a canon of governance, and distribute it throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the Veritable Records of Taizu and Taizong have been completed, I ask that ministers be charged to sift the worthy words and deeds they contain, and, following models such as the Zhenguan Essentials of Governance and the Hongwu Sacred Instructions, compile a book of governing principles for distribution throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 尤原萬幾之暇，朝夕省覽。

translations.literal: I especially hope that in leisure from myriad state affairs, Your Majesty will review it morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: Above all, I hope Your Majesty will set aside time from the press of affairs to read it morning and evening.

sentences.zh: 法開創之維艱，知守成之不易，何以用人而收群策之效？

translations.literal: Learning how arduous founding was and knowing how difficult maintaining achievements is—how may one employ men and harvest the effect of collective counsel?
translations.idiomatic: By learning how hard founding the dynasty had been and how difficult it is to preserve what has been won, how may one choose men wisely and draw benefit from counsel offered from every quarter?

sentences.zh: 何以納諫而宏虛受之風？

translations.literal: How may one accept remonstrance and expand the spirit of open receptivity?
translations.idiomatic: How may one welcome remonstrance and foster a spirit of generous listening?

sentences.zh: 何以理財而裕酌盈劑虛之方？

translations.literal: How may one manage finances and enrich the methods of balancing surplus and deficit?
translations.idiomatic: How may one manage the treasury and enlarge the means of balancing abundance against shortfall?

sentences.zh: 何以詳刑而無失出失入之患？

translations.literal: How may one examine punishments without the calamity of excessive or inadequate sentences?
translations.idiomatic: How may one judge criminal cases with care and avoid the errors of excessive leniency or excessive severity?

sentences.zh: 力行身體，則動有成模，紹美無極。」

translations.literal: If vigorously practiced in person, then actions will have models to follow and continuing excellence will know no limit."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty puts these lessons into practice yourself, every act will become a model, and the continuation of virtue will know no end."

sentences.zh: 上俞之，詔輯太祖、太宗聖訓，以機充纂修官。

translations.literal: The Emperor assented and ordered compilation of the Sacred Instructions of Taizu and Taizong, appointing Ji as compiler.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor approved and ordered the compilation of the Sacred Instructions of Taizu and Taizong, with Ji as chief editor.

sentences.zh: 累遷國史院侍讀學士，擢禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Reader in the Historiography Institute and elevated to Vice President of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to Reader of the Historiography Institute and was then appointed Vice President of Rites.

sentences.zh: 康熙六年，進尚書。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Kangxi, he was advanced to Minister.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 6 he was promoted to full minister.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「民窮之由有四：雜捐私派，棍徒哧詐，官貪而兵橫。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "There are four causes of the people's poverty: miscellaneous levies and private surcharges, club-wielding ruffians intimidating and swindling, and officials who are corrupt while soldiers are violent.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial: "The people's distress has four sources: assorted levies and unauthorized surcharges, thugs who intimidate and defraud, corrupt officials, and violent soldiers.

sentences.zh: 請嚴察督撫，舉劾當否，以息貪風、甦民命。

translations.literal: I request strict scrutiny of governors-general and governors, whether impeachments and commendations are proper, so as to quell the wind of corruption and revive the people's lives.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that governors-general and governors be strictly overseen and that their recommendations and impeachments be judged on their merits, so that corruption may be checked and the people relieved.

sentences.zh: 各省籓王、將軍、提、鎮有不法害民之事，許督撫糾劾。

translations.literal: In each province, if princes, generals, provincial military commanders, or regional commanders commit unlawful acts harmful to the people, governors-general and governors are permitted to impeach them.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever princes, garrison generals, provincial commanders, or regional commanders in the provinces commit unlawful acts that harm the people, governors should be allowed to impeach them.

sentences.zh: 請飭破除情私，毋更因循，貽誤地方。」

translations.literal: I request an order to eliminate personal favoritism, cease further procrastination, and avoid harming local administration."
translations.idiomatic: I urge that personal favoritism be swept away and that delay cease, lest local government continue to suffer."

sentences.zh: 七年，調戶部，再調吏部。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, he was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue and then again to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was moved to Revenue and then to Personnel.

sentences.zh: 機以疏通銓法、議降補官對品除用，為御史季振宜所劾。

translations.literal: Ji, for streamlining appointment regulations and proposing that officials appointed at reduced rank be used according to matched grade, was impeached by Censor Ji Zhenyi.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was impeached by Censor Ji Zhenyi for simplifying appointment rules and proposing that officials appointed at reduced rank be placed according to matched grade.

sentences.zh: 既而給事中王曰溫劾故庶吉士王彥即機子黃彥博，欺妄，應罷黜。

translations.literal: Then Supervising Secretary Wang Yuewen impeached the former Hanlin bachelor Wang Yan as Ji's son Huang Yanbo, alleging deceit; he should be dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Then Supervising Secretary Wang Yuewen accused the former Hanlin bachelor Wang Yan of being Ji's son Huang Yanbo, charged him with fraud, and demanded his dismissal.

sentences.zh: 機以彥與彥博姓名不同，且彥博死已久，疏辨，得免議。

translations.literal: Ji argued that Yan and Yanbo differed in name and that Yanbo had long been dead; in a memorial of defense he escaped censure.
translations.idiomatic: Ji replied in a memorial that Yan and Yanbo were not the same name and that Yanbo had died long ago, and thereby escaped further proceedings.

sentences.zh: 尋以遷葬乞假歸，而論者猶不已。

translations.literal: Soon he requested leave to return home to relocate burials, yet critics still did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: He soon took leave to return home for a reburial, but his critics still would not let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 十八年，特召還朝，以吏部尚書銜管刑部事。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, he was specially summoned back to court and, with the title of Minister of Personnel, managed the affairs of the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he was specially recalled to court and, holding the title of Minister of Personnel, was put in charge of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 御史張志棟言機老成忠厚，然衰邁，恐誤部事，應令罷歸。

translations.literal: Censor Zhang Zhidong said that Ji was seasoned and loyal, but decrepit, and feared he would mishandle ministry affairs; he should be dismissed and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Zhang Zhidong said that although Ji was experienced and loyal, he was now frail and might mishandle ministry business; he ought to be dismissed and sent home.

sentences.zh: 上以志棟言過當，命機供職如故。

translations.literal: The Emperor considered Zhang Zhidong's words excessive and ordered Ji to continue in office as before.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor judged Zhang's remarks excessive and ordered Ji to remain at his post.

sentences.zh: 明年，授吏部尚書。

translations.literal: The next year, he was appointed Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was appointed Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 以年老請告，詔慰留。

translations.literal: Citing old age, he requested leave; an edict comforted him and urged him to remain.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to retire on account of age, but the throne comforted him and kept him in office.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，拜文華殿大學士，兼吏部。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Hall of Literary Glory, concurrently holding the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he was made Grand Secretary of the Hall of Literary Glory while retaining the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 逾年，复乞休，許以原官致仕，遣官護行馳驛如故事。

translations.literal: After a year, he again begged to retire; he was permitted to retire at his original rank, and officials were dispatched to escort him post-haste according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he again asked to retire; he was allowed to leave at his existing rank, and escorts were sent to convey him home by relay post, as custom required.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，卒，諡文僖。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he died; his posthumous title was Wenxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year he died and was posthumously titled Wenxi.

sentences.zh: 宋德宜，字右之，江南長洲人。

translations.literal: Song Deyi, courtesy name Youzhi, was a native of Changzhou in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Song Deyi, styled Youzhi, came from Changzhou in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 父學朱，明御史，巡按山東，死於難。

translations.literal: His father Xuezhu was a censor of the Ming, inspector of Shandong, and died in calamity.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xuezhu had been a Ming censor and inspector of Shandong and died in the turmoil of the transition.

sentences.zh: 德宜年十七，伏闕請卹，與兄德宸、弟德宏並著文譽。

translations.literal: At seventeen, Deyi prostrated himself at the palace gate to request posthumous honors; together with his elder brother Dechen and younger brother Demi he was famed for literary reputation.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen Deyi knelt at the palace gate to seek honors for his father; he and his elder brother Dechen and younger brother Demi were all known for their literary gifts.

sentences.zh: 順治十二年，成進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Shunzhi he became a jinshi, was selected as Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 12 he passed the jinshi examination, entered the Hanlin, and was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 累遷國子監祭酒，嚴立條教，六館師生咸敬憚之。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Chancellor of the Imperial Academy, strictly established regulations, and teachers and students of the six halls all respected and feared him.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Chancellor of the Imperial Academy, where he imposed strict regulations; teachers and students throughout the six halls both respected and feared him.

sentences.zh: 聖祖親政，釋奠太學，禦彝倫堂，命德宜東鄉坐，講周易乾卦辭，稱旨。

translations.literal: When the Sage Ancestor personally assumed rule, he performed the libation sacrifice at the Imperial University, entered the Hall of Universal Principles, ordered Deyi to sit facing east, and lectured on the text of the Qian hexagram in the Book of Changes; this pleased the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor took personal rule, he offered sacrifice at the Imperial University, entered the Hall of Universal Principles, had Deyi sit facing east, and heard him expound the Qian hexagram of the Book of Changes—a performance that greatly pleased him.

sentences.zh: 遷翰林院侍讀學士，擢內閣學士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Reader in the Hanlin Academy and elevated to Grand Secretariat Academician.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Hanlin Reader and then elevated to Grand Secretariat Academician.

sentences.zh: 德宜風度端重，每奏事，輒當上意。

translations.literal: Deyi's bearing was dignified and grave; whenever he reported on affairs, he always hit the Emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Deyi was dignified in manner, and whenever he addressed the throne his words struck exactly the right note.

sentences.zh: 康熙十一年，扈蹕塞外，上從容詢及江南逋賦之由，德宜極言蘇、松賦役獨重，民力凋敝，上為動容。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Kangxi, while accompanying the imperial procession beyond the passes, the Emperor casually inquired into the causes of Jiangnan tax arrears. Deyi spoke fully of how the levies and corvée of Suzhou and Songjiang were uniquely heavy and the people's strength exhausted; the Emperor was moved.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 11, while accompanying the Emperor on tour beyond the Great Wall, he was asked in passing about the causes of Jiangnan's tax arrears. Deyi explained at length that Suzhou and Songjiang bore unusually heavy levies and that the people there were exhausted; the Emperor was visibly moved.

sentences.zh: 詔明年蠲蘇、松四府錢糧之半。

translations.literal: An edict remitted half the tax grain of the four prefectures of Suzhou and Songjiang the following year.
translations.idiomatic: The next year an edict remitted half the tax grain owed by the four prefectures of the Suzhou-Songjiang region.

sentences.zh: 遷戶部侍郎，發龍江關大使李九官餽遺，上嘉其不私，褫九官職。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice President of the Ministry of Revenue, exposed the gifts offered by Li Jiuguan, envoy of Longjiang Pass, and the Emperor praised his lack of partiality and stripped Jiuguan of office.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Vice President of Revenue, he exposed gifts offered by Li Jiuguan, the Longjiang Pass envoy; the Emperor praised his integrity and dismissed Jiuguan from office.

sentences.zh: 尋調吏部。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to Personnel.

sentences.zh: 十五年，擢左都御史。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, he was elevated to Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 時陝、甘、閩、粵漸已底定，惟吳三桂未平。

translations.literal: At the time Shaanxi-Gansu, Fujian-Guangdong were gradually pacified; only Wu Sangui remained unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: By then Shaanxi-Gansu and Fujian-Guangdong had been largely pacified; only Wu Sangui still held out.

sentences.zh: 德宜疏言：「三桂所恃，不過槍砲，槍砲專藉硝黃。

translations.literal: Deyi memorialized: "What Sangui relies on is nothing more than muskets and cannon; muskets and cannon depend entirely on saltpeter and sulfur.
translations.idiomatic: Deyi submitted a memorial: "Wu Sangui's strength rests on little more than muskets and cannon, and muskets and cannon depend wholly on saltpeter and sulfur.

sentences.zh: 硝黃產自河南、山西，必奸民圖利私販，請飭嚴禁。」

translations.literal: Saltpeter and sulfur are produced in Henan and Shanxi; scoundrels must be seeking profit through private trafficking. I request strict prohibition."
translations.idiomatic: Saltpeter and sulfur come from Henan and Shanxi, and unscrupulous men must be smuggling them for profit; I ask that the traffic be strictly forbidden."

sentences.zh: 上以督、撫、提、鎮稽察不嚴，下兵、刑二部嚴定處分。

translations.literal: Because governors-general, governors, provincial military commanders, and regional commanders had not supervised strictly enough, the Emperor referred the matter to the Ministries of War and Punishments to fix penalties strictly.
translations.idiomatic: Holding governors, provincial commanders, and regional commanders responsible for lax enforcement, the Emperor ordered the Ministries of War and Punishments to impose strict penalties.

sentences.zh: 德宜又疏言：「頻年發帑行師，度支不繼。

translations.literal: Deyi again memorialized: "In recent years treasury funds have been disbursed repeatedly for military campaigns, and revenue has not kept pace.
translations.idiomatic: Deyi submitted another memorial: "Campaign after campaign has drained the treasury, and revenue has not kept pace.

sentences.zh: 皇上允廷臣之請，開例捐輸。

translations.literal: Your Majesty acceded to the court ministers' request and opened a precedent for donation contributions.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, acceding to the ministers' request, opened the sale of offices by donation.

sentences.zh: 三年所入，二百萬有餘。

translations.literal: In three years the intake exceeded two million.
translations.idiomatic: In three years the receipts exceeded two million taels.

sentences.zh: 捐納最多者，莫如知縣，至五百餘人。

translations.literal: Among purchase appointments, none were more numerous than county magistrates, reaching more than five hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: No office was purchased more often than that of county magistrate; the number reached more than five hundred.

sentences.zh: 始因缺多易得，踴躍爭趨。

translations.literal: At first, because vacancies were many and appointment easy, people eagerly rushed to compete.
translations.idiomatic: At first, with many vacancies and easy appointment, men competed eagerly to buy in.

sentences.zh: 今見非數年不得選授，徘徊觀望。

translations.literal: Now they see that without several years they cannot be selected and appointed, and they hesitate and watch from the sidelines.
translations.idiomatic: Now, seeing that appointment may take years, they hang back and wait.

sentences.zh: 請敕部限期停止，慎重名器。」

translations.literal: I request that the ministry be ordered to halt the practice within a fixed term and treat prestigious offices with care."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the ministry be instructed to end the practice within a set deadline and treat official rank with due respect."

sentences.zh: 又疏言：「沿海居民，以漁為生。

translations.literal: He again memorialized: "Coastal residents live by fishing.
translations.idiomatic: In another memorial he wrote: "The people of the coast live by fishing.

sentences.zh: 佐賦稅，備災荒，而利用通商，又立市舶之制。

translations.literal: They supplement tax revenue, guard against famine and disaster, and through trade also benefit commerce; a system of maritime trade offices was therefore established.
translations.idiomatic: Their catch supports taxation and serves as a reserve against famine, while trade with the sea brings further benefit; for this reason the maritime trade office system was established.

sentences.zh: 本朝以海氛未靖，立禁甚嚴。

translations.literal: Our dynasty, because maritime disturbances were not yet settled, established prohibitions that were very strict.
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty, with the seas still unsettled, imposed very strict prohibitions.

sentences.zh: 近者日就蕩平，宜及此時招攜撫卹。

translations.literal: Recently matters have daily grown more settled; it is fitting at this time to win people over, comfort them, and provide relief.
translations.idiomatic: Now that calm is gradually returning, this is the moment to win the people over and extend relief.

sentences.zh: 沿海居民，以捕魚為業。

translations.literal: Coastal residents take fishing as their occupation.
translations.idiomatic: Coastal people make their living by fishing.

sentences.zh: 商人通販海島，皆許其造船出海，官給印票，仿舊例輸稅。

translations.literal: Merchants trading with island markets should all be permitted to build ships and go to sea; the government should issue sealed passes, and taxes should be paid according to former precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants trading with offshore islands should be allowed to build ships and put to sea; the government should issue official passes, and duties should be collected as in former times.

sentences.zh: 人口商貨，往來出入，咸稽核之。」

translations.literal: People, goods, and commerce going in and out should all be inspected and verified."
translations.idiomatic: All persons, cargo, and traffic in and out should be registered and checked."

sentences.zh: 事並下所司議行。

translations.literal: All these matters were referred to the responsible offices for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: All these proposals were referred to the appropriate offices for deliberation and action.

sentences.zh: 十七年，疏言：「自三桂煽亂，各路統兵大將軍以下，亦有玩寇殃民，營私自便。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, he memorialized: "Since Sangui stirred rebellion, among the commanders-in-chief and other officers leading troops on the various fronts, some have also treated the enemy lightly and harmed the people, seeking private advantage.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he submitted a memorial: "Since Wu Sangui's rebellion, even commanders-in-chief and other field officers have in some cases coddled the enemy, harmed the people, and pursued their own convenience.

sentences.zh: 或越省購買婦女，甚者掠奪民間財物，稍不如意，即指為叛逆。

translations.literal: Some cross provinces to purchase women; in extreme cases they plunder the people's property, and if slightly displeased they immediately denounce people as rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Some travel across provinces to buy women; worse still, they seize civilians' property, and at the least provocation denounce their victims as rebels.

sentences.zh: 今當剋期滅賊，尤恐藉端需索。

translations.literal: Now we are approaching the fixed date to destroy the rebels, and I especially fear they will use this as a pretext to extort demands.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the deadline to crush the rebels is near, I fear above all that officers will seize the occasion to extort and demand bribes.

sentences.zh: 請嚴飭。」

translations.literal: I request strict orders."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that strict orders be issued."

sentences.zh: 上下王大臣申禁。

translations.literal: Princes and ministers at every level proclaimed the prohibition.
translations.idiomatic: Princes and ministers throughout the court proclaimed the prohibition.

sentences.zh: 山東提督柯永蓁縱兵鼓譟，德宜劾奏，上命逮治。

translations.literal: Shandong Provincial Military Commander Ke Yongqin let his troops run riot with drums and clamor; Deyi memorialized impeaching him, and the Emperor ordered his arrest and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Ke Yongqin, provincial military commander of Shandong, allowed his troops to rampage noisily; Deyi impeached him in a memorial, and the Emperor ordered his arrest and trial.

sentences.zh: 孝昭皇后崩，德宜上疏請秉禮節哀，並言：「宵旰憂勤，天顏清減。

translations.literal: When Empress Xiaozhao died, Deyi submitted a memorial asking that mourning rites be observed and grief restrained, and also said: "Working from dawn till dusk in worry and diligence, Your Majesty's countenance has grown gaunt.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Xiaozhao died, Deyi submitted a memorial urging proper observance of mourning and restraint in grief, and wrote: "Your Majesty toils from dawn till dusk in anxious diligence, and your countenance has grown thin.

sentences.zh: 昔唐太宗銳意勤學，劉洎諫以多記損心。

translations.literal: In the past Emperor Taizong of Tang was keen to study diligently; Liu Ji remonstrated that excessive memorization harms the mind.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Emperor Taizong of Tang was eager to study without rest; Liu Ji remonstrated that too much memorization injures the mind.

sentences.zh: 宋儒程頤亦曰：『帝王之學，與儒生不同。』

translations.literal: The Song scholar Cheng Yi also said: 'The learning of emperors differs from that of Confucian scholars.'
translations.idiomatic: The Song scholar Cheng Yi also said: 'The learning of an emperor is not the same as that of a Confucian scholar.'

sentences.zh: 伏原紬繹篇章，略方名像數之繁，擇其有關政治、裨益身心者而討論之。

translations.literal: I humbly ask that Your Majesty study texts, setting aside the tedium of cosmological names and numerology, and select those relevant to governance and beneficial to body and mind for discussion.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly ask that Your Majesty read and reflect on texts, passing over the tedium of star names and numerology, and discuss only what bears on governance and nourishes body and mind.

sentences.zh: 稍節耳目之勞，用葆中和之德。」

translations.literal: Moderately reduce the labor of eyes and ears, thereby preserving the virtue of balanced harmony."
translations.idiomatic: Ease somewhat the strain on eyes and ears, and so preserve the virtue of balanced harmony."

sentences.zh: 上嘉納焉。

translations.literal: The Emperor commendably accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor praised and accepted the advice.

sentences.zh: 遷刑部尚書，調兵部。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Punishments, then to the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Minister of Punishments, then to the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 四川初定，大軍糗糧皆運自陝西，出棧道，顛踣相望，陝西民大困。

translations.literal: When Sichuan was first pacified, provisions for the great army were all transported from Shaanxi via the plank roads; overturned carts lay one after another in sight, and the people of Shaanxi were greatly distressed.
translations.idiomatic: When Sichuan was first pacified, grain for the main army was hauled entirely from Shaanxi over the plank roads; overturned carts lined the route, and the people of Shaanxi were sorely afflicted.

sentences.zh: 工部侍郎趙璟、金鼐疏上陳，德宜因言：「大軍下云、貴，需餉孔亟。

translations.literal: Vice Ministers of Works Zhao Jing and Jin Tai submitted memorials stating; Deyi therefore said: "The great army is descending on Yunnan and Guizhou; pay is urgently needed.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Ministers of Works Zhao Jing and Jin Tai submitted memorials on the matter; Deyi therefore wrote: "The main army is advancing into Yunnan and Guizhou, and supplies are urgently needed.

sentences.zh: 秦、蜀互相推諉，皆由總督分設。

translations.literal: Shaanxi and Sichuan mutually shift blame, all because governors-general are established separately.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi and Sichuan keep shifting blame onto each other, all because separate governors-general have been appointed.

sentences.zh: 川、陝設一總督，則痛癢相關，隨地調發，可以酌劑均平。」

translations.literal: If one governor-general were established for Sichuan and Shaanxi, then their pains and itches would be felt together; supplies could be mobilized according to locality, and disbursement could be weighed and balanced."
translations.idiomatic: If one governor-general were appointed for Sichuan and Shaanxi, each province would feel the other's distress; supplies could be mobilized locally, and burdens could be weighed and equalized."

sentences.zh: 詔如議行。

translations.literal: An edict ordered implementation as proposed.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered that the proposal be carried out.

sentences.zh: 靖逆將軍張勇以甘肅防邊事重，請緩裁前此添設官兵，部臣議如所請，德宜獨謂：「當日河東有兵事，添設官兵，事平應即裁汰。

translations.literal: Pacification General Zhang Yong, citing the importance of border defense in Gansu, requested postponing the reduction of recently added troops; ministry officials deliberated in accord with his request, but Deyi alone said: "At the time there was military action east of the Yellow River, so additional troops were added; once affairs were settled they should immediately have been reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification General Zhang Yong, citing the weight of Gansu border defense, asked that recently added troops not yet be cut; the ministry agreed, but Deyi alone argued: "Troops had been added when there was fighting east of the Yellow River; once peace returned they should at once have been reduced.

sentences.zh: 將軍標下前以步兵二千名改為馬兵，今宜復原，定經制馬六步四。

translations.literal: Under the general's command, two thousand infantry were previously converted to cavalry; now they should be restored to original form, fixing the established quota at six-tenths cavalry and four-tenths infantry.
translations.idiomatic: Under the general's command, two thousand infantry had been converted to cavalry; they should now be restored, with the established quota fixed at six parts horse and four parts foot.

sentences.zh: 惟以防邊添設之兵，無可議裁。」

translations.literal: Only the troops added for border defense cannot be debated for reduction."
translations.idiomatic: Only the troops added for border defense are not open to debate over reduction."

sentences.zh: 上遣尚書折爾肯往會勇等閱核，留河州、寧夏添設兵，餘仍復原定經制，如德宜議。

translations.literal: The Emperor dispatched Minister Zheerken to join Yong and others in inspection and verification; the added troops at Hezhou and Ningxia were retained, while the rest were restored to the original established quotas, as Deyi proposed.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent Minister Zheerken to join Zhang Yong and others in review; the added troops at Hezhou and Ningxia were kept, while the rest were restored to the original established quotas, as Deyi had urged.

sentences.zh: 迨三籓平，軍中俘獲婦女，並籍旗下。

translations.literal: When the Three Feudatories were pacified, women captured in the army were all registered under the banners.
translations.idiomatic: After the Three Feudatories were pacified, women taken captive in the army were all registered under the banners.

sentences.zh: 德宜言宜聽收贖，所釋甚眾。

translations.literal: Deyi said they should be permitted to redeem themselves; very many were released.
translations.idiomatic: Deyi argued that they should be allowed to ransom themselves; very many were freed.

sentences.zh: 調吏部。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 左都御史魏象樞、副都御史科爾昆等劾德宜會推江西按察使事失當，德宜疏辨，部議降五級。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Wei Xiangshu, Vice Censor-in-Chief Ke'erkun and others impeached Deyi for mishandling the joint recommendation of the Jiangxi Provincial Surveillance Commissioner; Deyi submitted a memorial in defense; the ministry recommended demotion by five ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Wei Xiangshu, Vice Censor-in-Chief Ke'erkun, and others impeached Deyi for mishandling the joint recommendation of a Jiangxi surveillance commissioner; Deyi defended himself in a memorial, and the ministry recommended demoting him five ranks.

sentences.zh: 上以會推原令各出所見，免德宜處分。

translations.literal: The Emperor held that joint recommendations originally allowed each to give his own view, and exempted Deyi from punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor held that joint recommendations were meant to allow each man his own view, and exempted Deyi from punishment.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，拜文華殿大學士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Hall of Literary Glory.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Hall of Literary Glory.

sentences.zh: 重修太宗實錄成，加太子太傅。

translations.literal: When the revised Veritable Records of Emperor Taizong were completed, he was given the additional title of Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When the revised Veritable Records of Emperor Taizong were completed, he was given the additional title of Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 德宜嚴毅木訥，然議國家大事，侃侃獨攄所見。

translations.literal: Deyi was stern, resolute, and taciturn, yet when discussing great affairs of state he spoke frankly and independently expressed his views.
translations.idiomatic: Deyi was stern and taciturn by nature, yet in debate over great affairs of state he spoke frankly and held to his own views.

sentences.zh: 居官廉謹，未仕時有宅一區，薄田數頃；

translations.literal: In office he was incorrupt and careful; before taking office he had one residence and a few acres of poor land;
translations.idiomatic: In office he was incorrupt and careful; before he entered service he owned one house and a few acres of poor land;

sentences.zh: 既貴，無所增益，門巷蕭然。

translations.literal: Once promoted to high rank, he added nothing; his gate and lane remained desolate.
translations.idiomatic: Once he rose to high rank he added nothing to them; his gate and lane remained bare.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，卒，諡文恪。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he died and was given the posthumous title Wenkè.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he died and was given the posthumous title Wenkè (Respectful and Prudent in Culture).

sentences.zh: 子駿業，自副貢授翰林院待詔，直御書處，歷兵科給事中。

translations.literal: His son Junye, from supplementary tribute graduate was appointed Hanlin Academy awaiting edicts, served at the Imperial Calligraphy Office, and rose to supervising secretary in the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: His son Junye, starting from supplementary tribute graduate, was appointed Hanlin awaiting edicts, served in the Imperial Calligraphy Office, and rose to supervising secretary in the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 康熙四十一年，疏劾湖廣總督郭琇、提督林本植、巡撫金璽、總兵雷如等辦理苗疆剿撫失宜，鞫實，琇等降革有差。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year of Kangxi, he memorialized impeaching Huguang Governor-General Guo Xiu, Provincial Military Commander Lin Benzhi, Governor Jin Xi, Regional Commander Lei Ru and others for mishandling the pacification and suppression of the Miao frontier; investigation confirmed the charges, and Xiu and the others were demoted or dismissed to varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-first year of Kangxi he memorialized against Huguang Governor-General Guo Xiu, provincial military commander Lin Benzhi, governor Jin Xi, regional commander Lei Ru, and others for mishandling the suppression and pacification of the Miao frontier; investigation confirmed the charges, and Xiu and the others were demoted or dismissed in varying degrees.

sentences.zh: 終兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: He ended as Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 伊桑阿，伊爾根覺羅氏，滿洲正黃旗人。

translations.literal: Yi Sang'a, of the Irgen Gioro clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Sang'a, of the Irgen Gioro clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 順治九年進士，授禮部主事。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the ninth year of Shunzhi, he was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of the ninth year of Shunzhi, he was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 累擢內閣學士。

translations.literal: He was promoted repeatedly to Grand Secretariat Academician.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted repeatedly until he became a Grand Secretariat Academician.

sentences.zh: 康熙十四年，遷禮部侍郎，擢​​工部尚書，調戶部。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Kangxi he was transferred to Vice Minister of Rites, promoted to Minister of Works, then transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Kangxi he was transferred to Vice Minister of Rites, promoted to Minister of Works, and then transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 時吳三桂踞湖南，廷議創舟師，自岳州入洞庭，斷賊餉道，命伊桑阿赴江南督治戰艦。

translations.literal: At the time Wu Sangui held Hunan; the court deliberated creating a naval force to enter Dongting from Yuezhou and cut the rebels' supply routes; Yi Sang'a was ordered to go to Jiangnan to supervise the construction of warships.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wu Sangui held Hunan; the court resolved to build a fleet to enter Dongting Lake from Yuezhou and cut the rebels' supply lines, and Yi Sang'a was ordered to Jiangnan to supervise construction of warships.

sentences.zh: 明年，復命偕刑部侍郎禪塔海詣茶陵督治戰艦。

translations.literal: The next year he was again ordered to go with Vice Minister of Punishments Chantaihai to Chaling to supervise warship construction.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was again ordered to go with Vice Minister of Punishments Chantaihai to Chaling to supervise warship construction.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，黃河決，命往江南勘視河工，以布政使崔維雅隨往，維雅條上治河法，與靳輔議不合。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year the Yellow River burst its banks; he was ordered to go to Jiangnan to inspect river works, with Provincial Administration Commissioner Cui Weiya accompanying; Weiya listed methods for river control that did not accord with Jin Fu's proposals.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year the Yellow River burst its banks; he was ordered to Jiangnan to inspect river works, accompanied by provincial administration commissioner Cui Weiya, who submitted a detailed plan for river control that did not accord with Jin Fu's proposals.

sentences.zh: 伊桑阿因請召輔面詢，上以維雅所奏無可行，寢之。

translations.literal: Yi Sang'a therefore requested summoning Fu for questioning in person; the Emperor held that what Weiya reported was not feasible and shelved it.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Sang'a therefore asked that Jin Fu be summoned for questioning in person; the Emperor found Weiya's proposals impracticable and set the matter aside.

sentences.zh: 尋疏陳黃河兩岸堤工修築不如式，奪輔職，戴罪督修。

translations.literal: Soon he memorialized that dikes on both banks of the Yellow River were not built to standard; Fu was stripped of office and ordered to supervise repairs while bearing guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he memorialized that dikes on both banks of the Yellow River had not been built to standard; Jin Fu was stripped of office and ordered to supervise repairs while bearing guilt.

sentences.zh: 復命籌海運，疏言：「黃河運道，非獨輸輓天庾，即商賈百貨，賴以通行，國家在所必治。

translations.literal: He was again ordered to plan sea transport and memorialized: "The Yellow River transport route not only conveys imperial grain but also allows merchants' goods of every kind to pass; the state must attend to it.
translations.idiomatic: He was again ordered to plan sea transport and wrote: "The Yellow River transport route not only carries imperial grain but also allows merchants' goods of every kind to pass; the state must maintain it.

sentences.zh: 若海運，先需造船，所費不貲；

translations.literal: As for sea transport, ships must first be built, at no small expense;
translations.idiomatic: Sea transport would first require building ships, at no small expense;

sentences.zh: 且膠、萊諸河久淤，開濬匪易。」

translations.literal: moreover the rivers of Jiao and Lai have long been silted up, and dredging them is no easy matter."
translations.idiomatic: moreover the rivers of Jiao and Lai have long been silted up, and dredging them would be no easy task."

sentences.zh: 上是之。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor approved this.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，俄羅斯犯邊，命往寧古塔造船備徵調。

translations.literal: That winter Russia violated the border; he was ordered to go to Ningguta to build ships in preparation for campaign mobilization.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, when Russia violated the border, he was ordered to Ningguta to build ships in preparation for mobilization.

sentences.zh: 再調吏部。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was again transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 二十三年夏，旱，偕王熙等清刑獄。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, summer, during drought, he joined Wang Xi and others in reviewing criminal cases.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year, during a summer drought, he joined Wang Xi and others in reviewing criminal cases.

sentences.zh: 其秋，扈蹕南巡，命閱視海口。

translations.literal: That autumn, accompanying the southern tour, he was ordered to inspect the river mouth.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, on the southern tour, he was ordered to inspect the river mouth.

sentences.zh: 疏言車路、串場諸河及白駒、草堰、丁溪諸口，宜飭河臣疏濬，引流入海。

translations.literal: He memorialized that the Chelu, Huanchang rivers and the outlets at Baiju, Caoyan, Dingxi and others should be ordered dredged by river officials to channel water into the sea.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that the Chelu and Huanchang rivers and the outlets at Baiju, Caoyan, Dingxi, and others should be dredged under orders to the river officials so that water could be channeled into the sea.

sentences.zh: 歷兵、禮二部尚書。

translations.literal: He served successively as Minister of War and Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as Minister of War and Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，拜文華殿大學士，兼吏部，充三朝國史總裁。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Hall of Literary Glory, concurrently heading the Ministry of Personnel, and served as chief compiler of the Three Reigns National History.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Hall of Literary Glory, concurrently headed the Ministry of Personnel, and served as chief compiler of the National History of Three Reigns.

sentences.zh: 三十六年，上親征噶爾丹，命往寧夏安設驛站，事平，與大學士阿蘭泰充平定朔漠方略總裁官。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year the Emperor personally campaigned against Galdan; Yi Sang'a was ordered to go to Ningxia to establish relay stations; when affairs were settled, he and Grand Secretary Arantai served as chief compilers of the Pacification of the Northern Deserts strategy record.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-sixth year the Emperor personally campaigned against Galdan; Yi Sang'a was ordered to Ningxia to establish relay stations; when the campaign ended, he and Grand Secretary Arantai served as chief compilers of the Pacification of the Northern Deserts strategy record.

sentences.zh: 居政府十五年，尤留意刑獄，每侍直勾本，上有所問，輒能舉其詞，同列服其精詳。

translations.literal: Having served in the government for fifteen years, he was especially attentive to criminal cases; whenever on duty reviewing capital sentences and the Emperor asked about a case, he could always recite the wording; his colleagues admired his precision and thoroughness.
translations.idiomatic: During fifteen years in high office he was especially attentive to criminal justice; whenever on duty reviewing capital sentences, if the Emperor asked about a case he could recite its wording from memory, and his colleagues admired his precision and thoroughness.

sentences.zh: 上嘗御批本房，伊桑阿與大學士王熙、吳琠及學士韓菼等以折本請旨，上曰：「人命至重，今當勾決，尤宜詳慎。

translations.literal: The Emperor once came in person to the memorial review office; Yi Sang'a with Grand Secretaries Wang Xi and Wu Yan and Academician Han Tan presented folded memorials requesting instructions; the Emperor said: "Human life is of utmost weight; today we are to confirm executions and must be especially thorough and careful.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor once came in person to the execution-review office; Yi Sang'a, Grand Secretaries Wang Xi and Wu Yan, and Academician Han Tan presented folded memorials for instruction; the Emperor said: "Human life is of the utmost weight; today we are to confirm executions, and must be especially thorough and careful.

sentences.zh: 爾等苟有所見，當盡言。」

translations.literal: If you have any views, you should speak fully."
translations.idiomatic: If you have any views, speak without reserve."

sentences.zh: 伊桑阿乃舉可矜疑者十餘人，皆得緩死，上徐曰：「此等所犯皆當死，猶曲求其可生之路，不忍輕斃一人。

translations.literal: Yi Sang'a then cited more than ten whose cases raised doubts deserving mercy; all received reprieve from death; the Emperor slowly said: "These offenses all warrant death, yet you still seek by every means paths by which they may live, unwilling lightly to execute a single person.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Sang'a then cited more than ten cases raising doubts deserving mercy; all received reprieve from death; the Emperor said slowly: "These men all committed offenses warranting death, yet you still seek by every means a path by which they may live, unwilling lightly to put a single man to death.

sentences.zh: 因念淮、揚百姓頻被水害，死者不知凡幾。

translations.literal: This brings to mind the people of Huai and Yang who have repeatedly suffered flood disasters, with dead beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: It brings to mind the people of Huai and Yang, who have repeatedly suffered floods, with dead beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 河患不除，朕不能暫釋於懷也！」

translations.literal: Until the river calamity is removed, I cannot briefly set it from my heart!"
translations.idiomatic: Until the river calamity is removed, I cannot set it briefly from my heart!"

sentences.zh: 伊桑阿陳災民困苦狀，上曰：「百姓既被水害，必至流離轉徙。

translations.literal: Yi Sang'a described the distress of disaster victims; the Emperor said: "Once the people have suffered flood disasters, they must wander and be displaced.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Sang'a described the distress of the disaster victims; the Emperor said: "Once the people have suffered flood disasters, they must wander and be displaced.

sentences.zh: 田多不耕，賦安從出？

translations.literal: Much land goes untilled; from what source can taxes come?
translations.idiomatic: Much land will go untilled; from what source can taxes come?

sentences.zh: 今當預免明年田賦，俾災黎於水退時思歸故鄉，粗安生業。」
