translations.literal: Now we should in advance exempt next year's land tax, so that disaster victims when the waters recede may think of returning to their native places and roughly restore their livelihoods."
translations.idiomatic: We should now exempt next year's land tax in advance, so that when the waters recede the afflicted may think of returning home and roughly restore their livelihoods."

sentences.zh: 伊桑阿等皆頓首，遂下詔免淮、揚明年田賦。

translations.literal: Yi Sang'a and the others all kowtowed; an edict was then issued exempting next year's land tax in Huai and Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Sang'a and the others all kowtowed, and an edict was then issued exempting next year's land tax in Huai and Yang.

sentences.zh: 三十七年，以年老乞休。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year, citing old age he requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-seventh year, citing old age, he requested retirement.

sentences.zh: 上諭阿蘭泰曰：「伊桑阿厚重老成，宣力年久。

translations.literal: The Emperor instructed Arantai: "Yi Sang'a is solid, weighty, and mature; he has served vigorously for many years.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor instructed Arantai: "Yi Sang'a is solid, weighty, and mature; he has served vigorously for many years.

sentences.zh: 爾二人自任閣事，推誠佈公，不惟朕知之，天下無不知者。

translations.literal: You two, since taking charge of Grand Secretariat affairs, have been sincere and fair in conduct; not only do I know this, but there is no one under heaven who does not.
translations.idiomatic: You two, since taking charge of Grand Secretariat affairs, have been sincere and fair in conduct; not only do I know this, but there is no one under heaven who does not.

sentences.zh: 伊桑阿雖年老求罷，朕不忍令去也。」

translations.literal: Though Yi Sang'a in old age seeks to withdraw, I cannot bear to let him go."
translations.idiomatic: Though Yi Sang'a in his old age seeks to withdraw, I cannot bear to let him go."

sentences.zh: 四十一年，復以病告，詔許原官致仕。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year he again reported illness; an edict permitted him to retire retaining his original rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-first year he again reported illness; an edict permitted him to retire with his original rank.

sentences.zh: 逾年卒，諡文端。

translations.literal: The following year he died and was given the posthumous title Wenduan.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he died and was given the posthumous title Wenduan (Correct in Culture).

sentences.zh: 乾隆中，入祀賢良祠。

translations.literal: During the Qianlong reign he was entered for worship in the Shrine of Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qianlong reign he was entered for worship in the Shrine of Worthies.

sentences.zh: 子伊都立，自舉人任內務府員外郎，歷刑部侍郎，巡撫山西。

translations.literal: His son Yiduli, from juren status served as Vice Director of the Imperial Household Department, rose to Vice Minister of Punishments, and served as Governor of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yiduli, starting from juren, served as vice director in the Imperial Household Department, rose to Vice Minister of Punishments, and served as governor of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 坐事奪職。

translations.literal: For an offense he was stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: For an offense he was stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 雍正七年，命赴大將軍傅爾丹軍治糧餉，授額外侍郎。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Yongzheng he was ordered to join General Furdan's army to manage provisions and pay, and was given the post of Extra Vice Minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Yongzheng he was ordered to General Furdan's army to manage provisions and pay, and was given the post of extra vice minister.

sentences.zh: 十三年，以侵蝕軍糧事覺，褫職下獄，論大辟。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year the embezzlement of military grain was discovered; he was stripped of office and imprisoned, sentenced to capital punishment.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year his embezzlement of military grain was discovered; he was stripped of office, imprisoned, and sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 乾隆七年，赦釋。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Qianlong he was pardoned and released.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Qianlong he was pardoned and released.

sentences.zh: 阿蘭泰，富察氏，滿洲鑲藍旗人。

translations.literal: Arantai, of the Fuca clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Arantai, of the Fuca clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 性敏慎。

translations.literal: By nature he was quick and cautious.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was quick and cautious.

sentences.zh: 初授兵部筆帖式。

translations.literal: He was first appointed a clerk in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was first appointed a clerk in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 康熙初，累遷職方郎中。

translations.literal: In the early Kangxi reign he was promoted repeatedly to Director in the Bureau of Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Kangxi reign he rose repeatedly until he became director in the Bureau of Appointments.

sentences.zh: 三籓事起，專司軍機文檄。

translations.literal: When the Three Feudatories rebellion arose, he was exclusively responsible for military dispatch documents.
translations.idiomatic: When the Three Feudatories rebellion broke out, he was put exclusively in charge of military dispatches.

sentences.zh: 議政王大臣以勤勞詳慎疏薦，得旨以三品卿用。

translations.literal: The Prince Regent and ministers recommended him in a memorial for diligence and careful thoroughness; he received an edict appointing him at third-rank ministerial level.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince Regent and ministers recommended him in a memorial for diligence and careful thoroughness; he received an edict appointing him at third-rank ministerial level.

sentences.zh: 二十年，擢光祿寺卿，遷內閣學士，充平定三逆方略副總裁，兼充明史總裁。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was promoted to Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, transferred to Grand Secretariat Academician, served as associate chief compiler of the Pacification of the Three Rebellions strategy record, and concurrently as chief compiler of the History of the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he was promoted to Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, transferred to Grand Secretariat Academician, served as associate chief compiler of the Pacification of the Three Rebellions strategy record, and concurrently as chief compiler of the History of the Ming.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，遷兵部侍郎，兼管佐領。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was transferred to Vice Minister of War, concurrently managing a company captaincy.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year he was transferred to Vice Minister of War, concurrently managing a company captaincy.

sentences.zh: 擢左都御史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 上閱方略，以敘事多舛錯，諭閣臣曰：「平逆始末，阿蘭泰知之甚詳，可與酌改，務期紀載得實。」

translations.literal: The Emperor perused the strategy record and, finding the narrative full of errors, instructed the Grand Secretariat ministers: "Arantai knows the beginning and end of the pacification rebellion in great detail; you may consult with him on revisions, striving to record the truth."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor read the strategy record and, finding the narrative full of errors, instructed the Grand Secretariat ministers: "Arantai knows the course of the pacification rebellion in great detail; consult with him on revisions, and see that the record accords with fact."

sentences.zh: 遷工部尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 累調吏部。

translations.literal: He was transferred repeatedly to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred repeatedly to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，上以雨澤愆期，命偕尚書徐元文慮囚，奏減罪可矜疑者四十五人。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, because rain was overdue, the Emperor ordered him together with Minister Xu Yuanwen to review prisoners; they memorialized reducing sentences for forty-five whose guilt was doubtful and deserving mercy.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year, because rain was overdue, the Emperor ordered him and Minister Xu Yuanwen to review prisoners; they memorialized reducing sentences for forty-five whose guilt was doubtful and deserving mercy.

sentences.zh: 是年拜武英殿大學士。

translations.literal: That year he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Hall of Martial Eminence.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Hall of Martial Eminence.

sentences.zh: 陝西飢，命阿蘭泰與河督靳輔議運江、淮糧米自黃河溯西安，以備積儲。

translations.literal: Shaanxi suffered famine; Arantai was ordered together with River Governor Jin Fu to discuss transporting Jiangnan and Huai grain up the Yellow River to Xi'an for reserve stores.
translations.idiomatic: When Shaanxi suffered famine, Arantai was ordered with River Governor Jin Fu to discuss transporting Jiangnan and Huai grain up the Yellow River to Xi'an for reserve stores.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，上出古北口巡歷塞外，命留京綜閱章奏。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year the Emperor went out through Gubeikou to tour beyond the passes; Arantai was ordered to remain in the capital to review memorials comprehensively.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fourth year the Emperor went out through Gubeikou to tour beyond the passes; Arantai was ordered to remain in the capital and review memorials comprehensively.

sentences.zh: 明年，上親征噶爾丹，阿蘭泰仍留京，與尚書馬齊、佛倫宿衛禁城。

translations.literal: The next year the Emperor personally campaigned against Galdan; Arantai still remained in the capital, lodging with Ministers Ma Qi and Folen to guard the Forbidden City.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the Emperor personally campaigned against Galdan; Arantai still remained in the capital, lodging with Ministers Ma Qi and Folen to guard the Forbidden City.

sentences.zh: 其秋，隨駕出歸化城，駐蹕黃河西界，經畫軍務。

translations.literal: That autumn he accompanied the imperial progress out of Guihuacheng, halting at the Yellow River's western border, planning military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he accompanied the imperial progress out of Guihuacheng, halting at the Yellow River's western border to plan military affairs.

sentences.zh: 以扈從勞，賜內廝馬。

translations.literal: For the toil of accompanying the progress he was granted an imperial stable horse.
translations.idiomatic: For the toil of accompanying the progress he was granted a horse from the imperial stables.

sentences.zh: 厄魯特台吉丹濟拉來降，上駐蹕翰特穆爾嶺，召入見，阿蘭泰及郎中阿爾法引之入禦幄，上屏左右，令阿蘭泰等出，獨與丹濟拉語良久。

translations.literal: The Oirat taiji Danjila came to surrender; the Emperor halted at Hantemer Ridge and summoned him for audience; Arantai and Director Alpha escorted him into the imperial tent; the Emperor dismissed attendants on both sides, ordered Arantai and the others out, and spoke alone with Danjila for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: When the Oirat taiji Danjila came to surrender, the Emperor halted at Hantemer Ridge and summoned him for audience; Arantai and Director Alpha escorted him into the imperial tent; the Emperor dismissed his attendants, ordered Arantai and the others out, and spoke alone with Danjila for a long time.

sentences.zh: 及退，召阿蘭泰諭曰：「爾偕降人入，以防不測，意甚善。

translations.literal: When they withdrew, he summoned Arantai and instructed: "You entered with the surrendering man to guard against the unexpected; your intention was very good.
translations.idiomatic: When they withdrew, he summoned Arantai and said: "You entered with the surrendering man to guard against the unexpected; your intention was very good.

sentences.zh: 朕令爾出，欲推誠示不疑耳。」

translations.literal: I ordered you out because I wished to show sincerity and signal that I did not doubt him."
translations.idiomatic: I ordered you out because I wished to show sincerity and signal that I did not doubt him."

sentences.zh: 三十七年，與伊桑阿俱以年老善忘奏解閣務，上曰：「大學士重任，必平坦雍和、任事謹慎者方為稱職。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year, together with Yi Sang'a he memorialized to resign from Grand Secretariat duties on account of age and forgetfulness. The Emperor said: "The post of Grand Secretary is a weighty charge; only one who is even-tempered and harmonious, and conducts affairs with caution, is fit for the office.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-seventh year he and Yi Sang'a memorialized to step down from Grand Secretariat duties, citing age and failing memory. The Emperor said: "The post of Grand Secretary is a weighty charge; only a man even-tempered and amiable, who handles affairs with scrupulous care, is truly fit for it.

sentences.zh: 至於記事，可令學士任之。」

translations.literal: As for keeping records, academicians may be assigned to it."
translations.idiomatic: As for keeping the minutes, that work may be left to academicians."

sentences.zh: 明年，卒。

translations.literal: The next year he died.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he died.

sentences.zh: 方病劇，上欲臨視，遣皇子先往，而阿蘭泰已卒。

translations.literal: When his illness grew grave, the Emperor wished to visit him in person and sent a prince ahead; but Arantai had already died.
translations.idiomatic: When his illness turned grave, the Emperor wished to visit him personally and sent a prince ahead—but Arantai was already dead.

sentences.zh: 上為輟朝一日，遣皇子及內大臣奠醊，贈太子太保，加贈少保，諡文清。

translations.literal: The Emperor suspended court for one day, sent a prince and an inner grand minister to offer libations, posthumously conferred Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, added posthumous conferral of Junior Guardian, and gave the posthumous title Wenqing.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor suspended court for a day, sent a prince and an inner grand minister to perform the libation rites, posthumously appointed him Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent with an additional conferral of Junior Guardian, and gave him the posthumous title Wenqing (Pure in Culture).

sentences.zh: 阿蘭泰操行清謹，處政府遠權勢，人莫敢干以私，以是為上所重。

translations.literal: Arantai's conduct was pure and careful; in the government he kept aloof from power and influence, and no one dared importune him for private ends; for this the Emperor valued him highly.
translations.idiomatic: Arantai's conduct was upright and meticulous; in office he kept his distance from power and influence, and no one dared approach him with private requests—qualities for which the Emperor held him in particular esteem.

sentences.zh: 後上與大學士論內閣舊臣，稱阿蘭泰能強記，且善治事云。

translations.literal: Later, when the Emperor discussed former Inner Cabinet ministers with grand secretaries, he praised Arantai's strong memory and skill in handling affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Later, discussing former Inner Cabinet ministers with the Grand Secretariat, the Emperor praised Arantai's remarkable memory and his skill in handling affairs.

sentences.zh: 子富寧安，初襲其從祖尼哈納拜他喇布勒哈番世職。

translations.literal: His son Funing'an initially inherited from his father's cousin Nihana the hereditary tabunang rank.
translations.idiomatic: His son Funing'an first inherited from a paternal cousin, Nihana, the hereditary tabunang rank.

sentences.zh: 自侍衛歷官正黃旗漢軍都統，改授左都御史，遷吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Starting as a guardsman, he served successively as Commandant of the Han Banner Eight Division of the Plain Yellow Banner, was reassigned as Censor-in-Chief of the Left, and was promoted to Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: From the Guard he rose to Commandant of the Han Military Eight Division of the Plain Yellow Banner, was reassigned Censor-in-Chief of the Left, and then promoted Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 富寧安內行修篤，事親至孝，聖祖亟稱之，又嘗諭廷臣曰：「富寧安自武員擢用，人皆稱其操守，是以授為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Funing'an's private conduct was cultivated and sincere; in serving his parents he was exceptionally filial, and the Sacred Ancestor frequently praised him. He also once instructed the court ministers: "Funing'an was promoted from a military officer; all speak well of his integrity—therefore he was appointed Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Funing'an's private life was disciplined and sincere, and in serving his parents he was exemplary in filial devotion; the Kangxi Emperor often praised him. He also once told the court: "Funing'an was promoted from the military ranks; everyone commends his integrity, which is why I made him Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 今部院中欲求清官甚難，當於初為筆帖式時，即念日後擢用，可為國家大臣，自立品行也。」

translations.literal: Today it is very hard to find honest officials among the ministries and boards; one should even when first serving as a clerk remember that he may later be promoted and become a great minister of state, and establish his character accordingly."
translations.idiomatic: Honest officials are scarce in the ministries and boards today; even at the first appointment as a clerk, a man should reflect that he may one day be promoted to high office and shape his character accordingly."

sentences.zh: 五十四年，策妄阿喇布坦侵哈密，命富寧安赴西寧視師，許以便宜調遣。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fourth year Tsewang Araptan invaded Hami; Funing'an was ordered to go to Xining to oversee the army, with permission to deploy troops at his discretion.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-fourth year, when Tsewang Araptan invaded Hami, Funing'an was ordered to Xining to oversee the campaign, with full discretion over deployments.

sentences.zh: 賊旋遁，詔緩進兵，回駐肅州，經理糧馬。

translations.literal: The rebels soon fled; an edict ordered a slower advance; he returned and encamped at Suzhou, supervising grain and horses.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels soon withdrew; he was ordered to slow the advance, returned to camp at Suzhou, and took charge of grain supplies and horses.

sentences.zh: 五十六年，授靖逆將軍，駐軍巴里坤，與將軍傅爾丹等分路規賊。

translations.literal: In the fifty-sixth year he was appointed Pacification General, encamped at Barkul, and with General Furdan and others planned against the enemy by separate routes.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-sixth year he was appointed Pacification General, stationed at Barkul, and with General Furdan and others devised converging operations against the enemy.

sentences.zh: 旋率兵襲擊厄魯特邊境，進屯烏魯木齊，屢敗賊。

translations.literal: He soon led troops in a raid on the Oirat border, advanced and encamped at Urumqi, and repeatedly defeated the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: He soon led troops in raids along the Oirat frontier, advanced to encamp at Urumqi, and repeatedly routed the enemy.

sentences.zh: 五十九年，進兵烏蘭烏蘇，遣侍衛哲爾德等分道襲擊，斬獲甚眾；

translations.literal: In the fifty-ninth year he advanced to Ulan Usu, dispatched Bodyguards Zhe'erde and others to strike by separate routes, and killed and captured in great numbers;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-ninth year he advanced on Ulan Usu, sent Bodyguards Zhe'erde and others on separate raids, and killed or captured large numbers of the enemy;

sentences.zh: 別遣散秩大臣阿喇納等諭降闢展回人，進擊吐魯番，降其酋長，獲駝馬無算。

translations.literal: Separately he dispatched Minister Without Portfolio Arana and others to persuade the Pichang Muslims to surrender, advanced to attack Turfan, received the surrender of its chieftains, and captured camels and horses beyond count.
translations.idiomatic: He separately dispatched Minister Without Portfolio Arana and others to accept the surrender of the Muslims of Pichang, pressed the attack on Turfan, received the submission of its chieftains, and seized camels and horses beyond numbering.

sentences.zh: 時策妄阿喇布坦挾所屬吐魯番回人偕徙，中道多遁歸，命富寧安收撫其眾。

translations.literal: At that time Tsewang Araptan had taken with him the Turfan Muslims under his rule in relocation; many fled back along the way; Funing'an was ordered to gather and settle the people.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Tsewang Araptan had withdrawn, taking the Turfan Muslims under his rule with him; many fled back along the route, and Funing'an was ordered to gather and settle them.

sentences.zh: 未幾，賊復來犯，遣將援剿，自率兵進駐伊勒布爾和碩，調遣策應。

translations.literal: Before long the enemy came to attack again; he dispatched generals to reinforce and suppress them, and himself led troops to advance and encamp at Ilebu Khot, coordinating deployments.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the enemy returned; he sent generals to reinforce the pursuit while he himself advanced to Ilebu Khot to coordinate the operation.

sentences.zh: 會阿喇納連敗賊，竄走，乃還駐巴里坤。

translations.literal: When Arana repeatedly defeated the enemy and they fled in rout, he returned to encamp at Barkul.
translations.idiomatic: When Arana routed the enemy in successive engagements and drove them into flight, Funing'an returned to camp at Barkul.

sentences.zh: 六十一年，疏言：「嘉峪關外、布隆吉爾之西，為古瓜、沙、燉煌地。

translations.literal: In the sixty-first year he memorialized: "West of Jiayuguan and Bulungir lies the ancient territory of Guazhou, Shazhou, and Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixty-first year he memorialized: "West of Jiayuguan and Bulungir lies the ancient territory of Guazhou, Shazhou, and Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 昔吐魯番建城屯種，遺址猶存，若駐兵屯牧，設總兵官一人統之，可扼黨色爾騰之路。」

translations.literal: Formerly Turfan built cities and established farming colonies; the sites still remain. If troops were encamped there for farming and grazing, with one brigade general to command them, the route through Dangse'erteng could be held."
translations.idiomatic: Turfan once built cities and established garrison farms there, and the ruins remain. Stationing troops to farm and graze livestock, under a single brigade general, would secure the route through Dangse'erteng."

sentences.zh: 又請專遣大臣領屯田糧儲及牧駝運糧事，上可其奏。

translations.literal: He also requested that a minister be specially dispatched to supervise agricultural colonies, grain stores, and camel transport of provisions; the Emperor approved his memorial.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that a minister be specially assigned to oversee garrison farming, grain stores, and the transport of provisions by camel herds; the Emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，授武英殿大學士，管軍務如故。

translations.literal: When the Shizong Emperor ascended the throne, Funing'an was appointed Grand Secretary of the Hall of Martial Eminence, continuing to manage military affairs as before.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yongzheng Emperor ascended the throne, he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Hall of Martial Eminence, with military affairs under his charge as before.

sentences.zh: 雍正四年，還朝，賜御用冠服、雙眼花翎、黃轡鞍馬，並諭王大臣：「富寧安端方廉潔，年來領兵將軍聲名無出其右者。」

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongzheng he returned to court, was granted imperial headgear and robes, double-eyed peacock plumes, and a yellow-bridled saddle horse, and the Emperor also instructed princes and grand ministers: "Funing'an is upright and incorruptible; among generals leading troops in recent years, none surpasses him in reputation."
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 4 he returned to court and was granted the Emperor's own robes and headgear, double-eyed peacock plumes, and a yellow-bridled saddle horse. The Emperor also told the princes and grand ministers: "Funing'an is upright and incorruptible; of the generals who have led troops in recent years, none stands higher in repute."

sentences.zh: 授世襲侯爵。

translations.literal: He was granted a hereditary marquisate.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted a hereditary marquisate.

sentences.zh: 尋進一等侯，加太子太傅，署西安將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to first-rank marquis, given the added title of Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, and appointed acting General of Xi'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon raised to first-rank marquis, made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, and appointed acting General of Xi'an.

sentences.zh: 六年，坐事奪爵，仍留大學士任。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, on account of an offense his peerage was stripped, but he remained in the post of Grand Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was stripped of his peerage for an offense but retained his post as Grand Secretary.

sentences.zh: 是年卒於西安，諡文恭，與父阿蘭泰同祀賢良祠。

translations.literal: That year he died at Xi'an; he was given the posthumous title Wengong and, together with his father Arantai, was enshrined in the Temple of Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He died at Xi'an that same year, received the posthumous title Wengong (Reverent in Culture), and was enshrined with his father Arantai in the Temple of Worthies.

sentences.zh: 徐元文，字公肅，江西崑山人。

translations.literal: Xu Yuanwen, courtesy name Gongsu, was a native of Kunshan in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yuanwen, styled Gongsu, was a native of Kunshan in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 初冒姓陸，通籍後復姓。

translations.literal: At first he assumed the surname Lu; after attaining official registration he restored his own surname.
translations.idiomatic: He had initially borne the surname Lu; after entering the ranks of office he restored his own family name.

sentences.zh: 少沉潛好學，與兄乾學、弟秉義有聲於時，稱為「三徐」。

translations.literal: From youth he was deep and reserved and loved learning; with his elder brother Qianxue and younger brother Bingyi he was famous in his time, and they were called "the Three Xus."
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was thoughtful and devoted to learning; with his elder brother Qianxue and younger brother Bingyi he won renown in his day, and the three were known as "the Three Xus."

sentences.zh: 元文舉順治十六年進士第一，世祖召見乾清門，還啟皇太后曰：「今歲得一佳狀元。」

translations.literal: Yuanwen took first place among jinshi in the sixteenth year of Shunzhi; the Shizu Emperor summoned him for audience at the Gate of Heavenly Purity; returning, he reported to the Empress Dowager: "This year we have gained an excellent zhuangyuan."
translations.idiomatic: Xu took first place in the jinshi examinations of Shunzhi 16; the Shizu Emperor received him in audience at the Gate of Heavenly Purity, and afterward told the Empress Dowager: "This year we have an outstanding zhuangyuan."

sentences.zh: 賜冠帶、蟒服，授翰林院修撰。

translations.literal: He was granted headgear and girdle, python robes, and appointed Compiler of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted court robes and python insignia and appointed Compiler of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 從幸南苑，賜乘御馬。

translations.literal: Accompanying the Emperor on a visit to the Southern Park, he was granted permission to ride an imperial horse.
translations.idiomatic: On accompanying the Emperor to the Southern Park, he was granted the use of an imperial horse.

sentences.zh: 嘗奉命撰孚齋說，孚齋，世祖讀書所也，上覽之稱善，命刊行。

translations.literal: He was once ordered to compose the "Fu Studio Discourse"; the Fu Studio was the Shizu Emperor's place of study; the Emperor, on reading it, praised it and ordered it published.
translations.idiomatic: He was once ordered to compose the Discourse on the Fu Studio—the Shizu Emperor's study; the Emperor read it with approval and ordered it published.

sentences.zh: 康熙初，江南逋賦獄起，元文名麗籍中，坐謫鑾儀衛經歷，事白，復原官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kangxi a case of tax arrears arose in Jiangnan; Yuanwen's name appeared on the roster; he was demoted to Director in the Imperial Procession Guard; when the matter was cleared, he was restored to his original post.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kangxi reign a case of tax arrears erupted in Jiangnan; Xu's name appeared on the suspect list, and he was demoted to Director in the Imperial Procession Guard; when the affair was cleared, he was restored to his former rank.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，居喪行古禮。

translations.literal: Upon his father's death he entered mourning and observed the ancient rites.
translations.idiomatic: Upon his father's death he entered mourning and observed the ancient funeral rites in full.

sentences.zh: 起補國史院修撰，累遷國子監祭酒，充經筵講官。

translations.literal: Called back to service, he was appointed Compiler of the State History Academy, was repeatedly promoted to Chancellor of the Imperial Academy, and served as lecturer on the classics mat.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to office, he was appointed Compiler of the State History Academy, rose in stages to Chancellor of the Imperial Academy, and served as lecturer on the classics mat.

sentences.zh: 元文閒雅方重，音吐宏暢，進講輒稱旨。

translations.literal: Yuanwen was easy and elegant, dignified and weighty; his voice was broad and clear; whenever he lectured it pleased the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Xu was refined and dignified, with a full and resonant voice; his lectures on the classics invariably pleased the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 元文疏請「敕直省學臣間歲一舉優生，鄉試仍復副榜額，俱送監肄業」。

translations.literal: Yuanwen memorialized requesting: "Order provincial education commissioners every other year to select distinguished students; restore the supplementary provincial examination quotas, and send all to study at the Imperial Academy."
translations.idiomatic: Xu memorialized requesting that provincial education commissioners be ordered to select distinguished students every other year, that the supplementary provincial examination quota be restored, and that the chosen scholars be sent to study at the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 並著為令。

translations.literal: This was also enacted as a regulation.
translations.idiomatic: These measures were enacted as permanent regulations.

sentences.zh: 復請永停納粟，章下所司。

translations.literal: He again requested the permanent abolition of grain-donation degrees; the memorial was referred to the relevant offices.
translations.idiomatic: He further asked that the sale of degrees by grain donation be permanently halted; the memorial was referred to the relevant offices.

sentences.zh: 居國學四年，端士習，正文體，條教大飭。

translations.literal: During four years at the Imperial Academy he rectified student conduct, corrected literary style, and greatly tightened regulations.
translations.idiomatic: In four years at the Imperial Academy he restored proper student conduct, corrected literary style, and tightened discipline throughout.

sentences.zh: 其後上語閣臣：「徐元文為祭酒，規條嚴肅。

translations.literal: Later the Emperor told grand secretaries: "When Xu Yuanwen served as Chancellor, his regulations were strict and solemn.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Emperor told the Grand Secretariat: "As Chancellor, Xu Yuanwen ran the Academy with strict and solemn regulations.

sentences.zh: 滿洲子弟不率教者，輒加撻責，咸敬憚之，後人不能及也。」

translations.literal: Manchu students who failed to obey instruction were promptly flogged; all feared and respected him—later men could not equal him."
translations.idiomatic: Manchu students who misbehaved were promptly flogged; all feared and respected him—a rigor none of his successors matched."

sentences.zh: 十三年，遷內閣學士，改翰林院掌院學士，充日講起居注官，教習庶吉士。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was transferred to Academician of the Grand Secretariat, reassigned Academician of the Hanlin Academy in charge of the academy, served as diarist for the Daily Lecture, and instructed advanced scholars.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was transferred to Academician of the Grand Secretariat, reassigned Chief Academician of the Hanlin Academy, served as diarist for the Daily Lecture, and tutored advanced scholars.

sentences.zh: 先是熊賜履在講筵，累稱說孔、孟、程、朱之道，上欲博覽前代得失之由，命詞臣以通鑑與四書參講。

translations.literal: Earlier Xiong Cifu had lectured at the classics mat, repeatedly expounding the ways of Confucius, Mencius, Cheng, and Zhu; the Emperor wished broadly to survey the causes of success and failure in past ages and ordered the literary officials to interweave lectures on the Comprehensive Mirror with the Four Books.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Xiong Cifu had lectured at the classics mat, expounding again and again the teachings of Confucius, Mencius, the Cheng brothers, and Zhu Xi; wishing to survey broadly how past dynasties had risen and fallen, the Emperor ordered the literary officials to lecture on the Comprehensive Mirror in conjunction with the Four Books.

sentences.zh: 元文因取朱子綱目，擇其事之系主德、裨治道者，採取先儒之說，參以臆斷，演繹發揮，按期進講。

translations.literal: Yuanwen thereupon took Zhu Xi's Outline and Discourses, selected events bearing on sovereign virtue and useful to governance, drew on the sayings of earlier sages, supplemented them with his own judgments, elaborated and developed them, and delivered lectures on schedule.
translations.idiomatic: Xu thereupon drew on Zhu Xi's Outline and Discourses, selecting events bearing on sovereign virtue and good governance, weaving in earlier sage-commentary and his own judgments, and delivered his lectures on schedule.

sentences.zh: 尋以母憂歸。

translations.literal: Soon he returned home on account of his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: He soon withdrew to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 十八年，特召監修明史，疏請徵求遺書，薦李清、黃宗羲、曹溶、汪懋麟、黃虞稷、姜宸英、萬言等，徵入史館，不至者，錄所著書以上。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was specially summoned to supervise compilation of the History of the Ming; he memorialized requesting the collection of lost books and recommended Li Qing, Huang Zongxi, Cao Rong, Wang Maolin, Huang Yuqi, Jiang Chenying, Wan Yan, and others; those summoned to the History Office who did not come had their works copied and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he was specially summoned to supervise the History of the Ming; he memorialized requesting lost books be sought out and recommended Li Qing, Huang Zongxi, Cao Rong, Wang Maolin, Huang Yuqi, Jiang Chenying, Wan Yan, and others; those who did not enter the History Office had their writings copied and submitted instead.

sentences.zh: 尋補內閣學士。

translations.literal: Soon he was made up as Academician of the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Academician of the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時有議遣大臣巡方者，元文言於閣中曰：「巡方向遣御史，以有台長約束，故僨事者鮮。

translations.literal: At that time there was discussion of dispatching grand ministers on provincial inspection tours; Yuanwen said within the Grand Secretariat: "Provincial tours have been assigned to censors, who are held in check by their bureau chiefs—therefore failures have been few.
translations.idiomatic: When some proposed dispatching grand ministers on provincial inspection tours, Xu said within the Grand Secretariat: "Such tours are properly assigned to censors, who answer to their bureau chiefs—hence few have abused their authority.

sentences.zh: 若遣大臣，或妄作威福，誰能禁之？」

translations.literal: If grand ministers are dispatched, some may presumptuously wield authority and privilege—who could restrain them?"
translations.idiomatic: Send a grand minister instead, and he may presumptuously lord it over the provinces—who could stop him?"

sentences.zh: 因入告，事得寢。

translations.literal: He then entered and reported this; the proposal was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: He reported this to the Emperor, and the proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 明年，擢左都御史。

translations.literal: The next year he was promoted to Censor-in-Chief of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was promoted Censor-in-Chief of the Left.

sentences.zh: 會師下雲南，吳三桂之徒多率眾歸附，耗餉不貲。

translations.literal: Just then the army descended on Yunnan; many of Wu Sangui's followers came over with their forces in submission, consuming provisions beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: As the army pressed into Yunnan, many of Wu Sangui's followers submitted with their forces, consuming supplies beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 元文疏言：「三桂遺孽，旦夕伏誅。

translations.literal: Yuanwen memorialized: "The remnants of Sangui will be executed within days.
translations.idiomatic: Xu memorialized: "Sangui's remaining followers will be executed any day now.

sentences.zh: 凡脅從之眾，恩許自新。

translations.literal: All who followed under compulsion should be granted mercy to renew themselves.
translations.idiomatic: All who followed under duress should be allowed to start anew under imperial grace.

sentences.zh: 若仍留本土，既非永久之規；

translations.literal: If they remain in their native places, that is no permanent plan;
translations.idiomatic: To leave them in their native places is no lasting solution;

sentences.zh: 移調他方，亦多遷徙之費。

translations.literal: to transfer them elsewhere also entails heavy costs of relocation.
translations.idiomatic: yet transferring them elsewhere entails heavy resettlement costs.

sentences.zh: 統以別將，則猜疑未化，終涉危嫌；

translations.literal: To place them under separate generals leaves suspicion undispelled and ultimately invites dangerous mistrust;
translations.idiomatic: Assigning them to separate commanders leaves suspicion undispelled and invites dangerous mistrust;

sentences.zh: 攝之歸旗，則放恣既久，猝難約束。

translations.literal: to absorb them back into the banners means that, having been unrestrained so long, they cannot suddenly be controlled.
translations.idiomatic: absorbing them back into the banners means that, after years of license, they cannot be controlled overnight.

sentences.zh: 請以武職及入伍者，與綠旗一體錄用。

translations.literal: I request that those qualified for military office and those already enlisted be employed on the same terms as Green Standard troops.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that men qualified for military office and those already enlisted be employed on the same terms as Green Standard troops.

sentences.zh: 餘俱分遣為民，以裕餉需。

translations.literal: The remainder should all be dispersed as commoners to ease the burden on provisions.
translations.idiomatic: The rest should be released to civilian life to ease the strain on military supplies.

sentences.zh: 至耿精忠、尚之信、孫延齡舊隸將弁，尤宜解散，勿仍籓旗名目。」

translations.literal: As for officers and soldiers formerly under Geng Jingzhong, Shang Zhixin, and Sun Yanling, they should especially be disbanded and no longer kept under feudatory banner designations."
translations.idiomatic: As for officers and soldiers formerly under Geng Jingzhong, Shang Zhixin, and Sun Yanling, they should be disbanded altogether and no longer kept under feudatory banner designations."

sentences.zh: 又請「革三籓虐政，在粵者五：曰鹽埠，曰渡稅，曰總店，曰市舶，曰魚課；

translations.literal: He also requested: "Abolish the Three Feudatories' oppressive exactions—in Guangdong five: salt monopolies, ferry tolls, general stores, maritime trade levies, and fishing dues;
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that the Three Feudatories' oppressive exactions be abolished—in Guangdong five: salt monopolies, ferry tolls, general stores, maritime trade levies, and fishing dues;

sentences.zh: 在閩者四：曰鹽稅，曰報船，曰冒擾驛夫，曰牙行渡稅；

translations.literal: in Fujian four: salt taxes, reporting-ship fees, unauthorized requisition of post station laborers, and broker ferry taxes;
translations.idiomatic: in Fujian four: salt taxes, reporting-ship fees, unauthorized requisition of post station laborers, and broker ferry taxes;

sentences.zh: 在滇者四：曰勳莊，曰圈田，曰礦廠，曰冗兵。」

translations.literal: in Yunnan four: fief estates, enclosed fields, mining concessions, and redundant soldiers."
translations.idiomatic: in Yunnan four: fief estates, enclosed fields, mining concessions, and redundant soldiers."

sentences.zh: 疏入，俱下所司議行。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, all items were referred to the relevant offices for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: On submission, every item was referred to the relevant offices for deliberation and implementation.

sentences.zh: 初，御史劉安國請察隱佔田畝，州縣利有升敘，多捏報累民。

translations.literal: Earlier Censor Liu Anguo had requested investigation of concealed land holdings; because prefectures and counties stood to gain promotions for reporting results, many fabricated reports and burdened the people.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Censor Liu Anguo had proposed investigating concealed land holdings; because local officials stood to gain promotion for uncovering such cases, many fabricated reports and burdened the people.

sentences.zh: 元文力言其弊，謂名為加稅，實耗糧戶。

translations.literal: Yuanwen forcefully stated its abuses, saying that though called additional taxation, it in fact drained grain-paying households.
translations.idiomatic: Xu spoke forcefully against the abuse, arguing that though labeled additional taxation, it in fact drained grain-paying households.

sentences.zh: 請飭督撫檢舉，复條​​列近時督撫四弊。

translations.literal: He requested that governors-general and governors be ordered to investigate and report, and also itemized four abuses of recent governors-general and governors.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that governors-general and governors be ordered to investigate and report, and also itemized four recent abuses among provincial governors.

sentences.zh: 時部例捐納官到任三年後稱職者，具題升轉；

translations.literal: At that time ministerial regulations provided that purchased offices, after three years in post if deemed competent, should be submitted for promotion;
translations.idiomatic: At that time regulations provided that officials who had purchased their posts, if deemed competent after three years, should be submitted for promotion;

sentences.zh: 不稱職者，罷之。

translations.literal: those deemed incompetent were to be dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: the incompetent were to be dismissed.

sentences.zh: 既，復令捐銀者免其具題，又生員得捐納歲貢。

translations.literal: Subsequently, however, those who donated silver were exempted from such submission; moreover, licentiates were permitted to purchase tribute-student status by donation.
translations.idiomatic: Later, however, donors of silver were exempted from review, and licentiates were allowed to purchase tribute-student status.

sentences.zh: 元文言捐納事例，系一時權宜，請於收復滇南之日，降詔停止，言甚剴切。

translations.literal: Yuanwen said the donation regulations were a temporary expedient and requested that on the day Yunnan was recovered an edict be issued halting them; his language was very earnest.
translations.idiomatic: Xu argued that the donation regulations were a temporary expedient and earnestly asked that an edict halt them on the day Yunnan was recovered.

sentences.zh: 雲南平，告廟肆赦，廷臣多稱頌功德。

translations.literal: When Yunnan was pacified, the Emperor reported to the ancestral temple and proclaimed a general amnesty; court ministers largely praised his achievements and virtue.
translations.idiomatic: When Yunnan was pacified, the Emperor reported to the ancestral temple and proclaimed a general amnesty; court ministers largely praised his achievements.

sentences.zh: 元文獨言：「聖人作易，於泰、豐、既濟諸卦，垂戒尤切。

translations.literal: Yuanwen alone said: "When the sage made the Changes, in the hexagrams Tai, Feng, Jiji, and others, he set forth admonitions especially urgent.
translations.idiomatic: Xu alone said: "When the sage compiled the Changes, the hexagrams Tai, Feng, and Jiji carry warnings of special urgency.

sentences.zh: 景運方新，原皇上倍切諮儆。

translations.literal: Our bright fortune is newly risen; I pray Your Majesty will doubly heed counsel and vigilance.
translations.idiomatic: Our good fortune is newly risen; I pray Your Majesty will be doubly vigilant against complacency.

sentences.zh: 兼諭大小臣工，洗心滌慮，毗贊大業。

translations.literal: Also instruct ministers great and small to cleanse their hearts and purge their thoughts, and assist the great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Exhort ministers great and small to cleanse their hearts and assist this great enterprise.

sentences.zh: 勿狃目前之淺圖，務培國家之元氣。

translations.literal: Do not cling to shallow designs of the moment; strive to cultivate the state's vital force.
translations.idiomatic: Do not cling to shallow expedients of the moment; strive to nourish the nation's vital strength.

sentences.zh: 振紀綱以崇大體，核名實以課吏材，崇清議以定國是，厲廉恥以正人心，端教化以圖治本，抑營競以儆官邪，敦節儉以厚風俗，正名分以絕姦萌，並當今急務。」

translations.literal: Reviving discipline to honor the great foundations, verifying names and realities to assess officials' talents, honoring pure opinion to fix the nation's course, promoting integrity and shame to rectify the human heart, rectifying education to seek the root of order, restraining self-seeking rivalry to warn against official corruption, encouraging thrift to enrich custom, and correcting names and ranks to cut off the seeds of treachery—these are all urgent tasks of the present day."
translations.idiomatic: Restoring discipline to honor the foundations of rule, matching names to realities to test officials' merit, honoring honest debate to settle the nation's course, promoting integrity and shame to rectify hearts, restoring education to secure lasting order, restraining selfish ambition to warn against official corruption, encouraging thrift to strengthen custom, and keeping names and ranks in proper order to cut off treachery at the root—all are urgent tasks of the day."

sentences.zh: 上俞之。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 時方嚴窩逃之禁，杭州將軍馬哈達以民間多匿逃人，請自句攝，勿移有司。

translations.literal: At that time the ban on harboring fugitives was strictly enforced; Hangzhou General Mahata, citing many hidden fugitives among the populace, requested to summon and arrest them himself without referring the matter to civil authorities.
translations.idiomatic: At that time enforcement of the ban on harboring fugitives was strict; Hangzhou General Mahata, noting many fugitives hidden among the populace, asked to conduct arrests himself without involving the civil authorities.

sentences.zh: 元文曰：「是重擾民也。

translations.literal: Yuanwen said: "That would greatly disturb the people.
translations.idiomatic: Xu said: "That would greatly disturb the people.

sentences.zh: 無已，當令督撫會同將軍行之。」

translations.literal: If it cannot be avoided, the governor-general and governor should be ordered to act jointly with the general."
translations.idiomatic: If it must be done, let the governor-general and governor act jointly with the general."

sentences.zh: 京師奸人，多掠平民賣旗下，官吏豫印空契給之，屢發覺，元文疏請禁止。

translations.literal: In the capital rogues often seized commoners and sold them into banner households; officials pre-stamped blank contracts for them; this was repeatedly exposed; Yuanwen memorialized requesting a ban.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital, scoundrels often kidnapped commoners and sold them into banner households, with officials supplying pre-stamped blank contracts; after repeated exposures, Xu memorialized requesting a ban.

sentences.zh: 又八旗家人投水、自經，報部者歲及千人，疏請嚴定處分。

translations.literal: Also, banner household bondservants who drowned themselves or hanged themselves—those reported to the ministry reached a thousand per year; he memorialized requesting strict fixed penalties.
translations.idiomatic: He also noted that banner bondservants who drowned or hanged themselves—cases reported to the ministry—reached a thousand a year, and memorialized requesting strict fixed penalties.

sentences.zh: 上俱從之。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved all.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor approved all.

sentences.zh: 京察計典罷官者，謀入貲捐复，元文力持不可，遂罷議。

translations.literal: Officials dismissed in the capital evaluation cycle plotted to restore themselves by donating funds; Yuanwen forcefully held that this was impermissible, and the proposal was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Officials dismissed in the capital evaluation cycle sought to restore themselves through donations; Xu forcefully objected, and the proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 先後疏劾福建總督姚啟聖縱恣譎詐，杭州副都統高國相縱兵虐民，兩淮巡鹽御史堪泰徇庇貪官，御史蕭鳴鳳居喪蔑禮，俱讞鞫得實，惟啟聖辨釋。

translations.literal: In succession he memorialized to impeach Fujian Governor-General Yao Qisheng for wantonness and cunning deceit, Hangzhou Vice Commander-in-Chief Gao Guoxiang for letting troops abuse the people, Lianghu Salt Censor Kantai for shielding corrupt officials, and Censor Xiao Mingfeng for contempt of mourning rites—all were reviewed and tried and found true, except Qisheng, who was cleared on explanation.
translations.idiomatic: He successively impeached Fujian Governor-General Yao Qisheng for arrogance and deceit, Hangzhou Vice Commander-in-Chief Gao Guoxiang for allowing troops to abuse the people, Lianghu Salt Censor Kantai for shielding corrupt officials, and Censor Xiao Mingfeng for violating mourning rites—all were investigated and found guilty, except Qisheng, who was cleared on appeal.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，以會推湖北按察使，坐所舉不實，鐫三秩調用。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, in the collective recommendation for Hubei Judicial Commissioner, he was charged with recommending unreliably and was demoted three ranks and transferred.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year he was charged with unreliable recommendations in the collective selection for Hubei Judicial Commissioner, demoted three ranks, and transferred.

sentences.zh: 尋命專領史局。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to supervise the History Office exclusively.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered to supervise the History Office exclusively.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，复代其兄乾學為左都御史，遷刑部尚書，調戶部。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he again replaced his elder brother Qianxue as Censor-in-Chief of the Left, was transferred to Minister of Justice, and then to Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year he again replaced his elder brother Qianxue as Censor-in-Chief of the Left, was appointed Minister of Justice, and then transferred to Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，拜文華殿大學士，兼掌翰林院事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Hall of Literary Glory and concurrently directed the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Hall of Literary Glory and given concurrent charge of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 上南巡，幸蘇州，以江南浮糧太重，有旨詢戶部。

translations.literal: When the Emperor made a southern tour and visited Suzhou, because Jiangnan's surplus grain levies were too heavy, an edict inquired of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: On the Emperor's southern tour to Suzhou, noting that Jiangnan's surplus grain levies were excessively heavy, he issued an edict inquiring of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 元文考宋、元以來舊額官田、民田始末及前明歷代詔書以聞。

translations.literal: Yuanwen investigated the origins and development of official and private land quotas since Song and Yuan and the proclamations of successive Ming reigns, and reported.
translations.idiomatic: Xu investigated the origins of official and private land quotas since Song and Yuan and the proclamations of successive Ming reigns, and reported his findings.

sentences.zh: 元文在內閣，上复諭及之，元文頓首曰：「聖明及此，三吳之福也。」

translations.literal: When Yuanwen was in the Grand Secretariat, the Emperor again raised the matter and instructed him; Yuanwen kowtowed and said: "Your sage clarity reaches even to this—blessing for the Three Wu region.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu was in the Grand Secretariat, the Emperor raised the matter again; Xu kowtowed and said: "That Your Majesty's wisdom extends even to this is a blessing for the Three Wu region.

sentences.zh: 因下九卿議，有力尼之者，事遂寢。

translations.literal: The matter was therefore referred to the Nine Ministers for deliberation, but powerful men obstructed it and the proposal was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was therefore referred to the Nine Ministers for deliberation, but powerful men obstructed it and the proposal was shelved.

sentences.zh: 元文兄乾學，豪放，頗招權利，坐論罷；

translations.literal: Yuanwen's elder brother Qianxue was bold and unrestrained, gathered power and profit rather freely, and was dismissed after impeachment;
translations.idiomatic: Yuanwen's elder brother Qianxue was bold and unrestrained, gathered power and profit rather freely, and was dismissed after impeachment;

sentences.zh: 而元文謹禮法，門庭肅然。

translations.literal: Yuanwen, by contrast, was strict in ritual and law, and his household gate was solemn and orderly.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanwen, by contrast, was strict in ritual and law, and his household was solemn and orderly.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，兩江總督傅拉塔劾乾學子侄交結巡撫洪之傑，招權競利，詞連元文，上置不問，予元文休致回籍。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, Liangjiang Governor-General Fulata impeached Qianxue's sons and nephews for colluding with Governor Hong Zhijie to gather power and compete for profit; the accusation implicated Yuanwen, but the emperor set it aside and granted Yuanwen retirement to return home.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year, Liangjiang Governor-General Fulata impeached Qianxue's sons and nephews for colluding with Governor Hong Zhijie to gather power and compete for profit; the accusation implicated Yuanwen, but the emperor set it aside and granted Yuanwen retirement to return home.

sentences.zh: 舟過臨清，關吏大索，僅圖書數千卷，光祿饌金三百而已。

translations.literal: When his boat passed Linqing, customs officers searched thoroughly and found only several thousand volumes of books and three hundred taels of provision money from the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: When his boat passed Linqing, customs officers searched thoroughly and found only several thousand volumes of books and three hundred taels of provision money from the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 家居一年卒。

translations.literal: After a year at home he died.
translations.idiomatic: After a year at home he died.

sentences.zh: 乾學自有傳。

translations.literal: Qianxue has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Qianxue has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 弟秉義，字彥和，舉康熙十二年進士第三，授編修，遷右中允。

translations.literal: His younger brother Bingyi, style name Yanhe, placed third in the jinshi examination of the twelfth year of Kangxi, was appointed compiler, and was transferred to Right Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Bingyi, courtesy name Yanhe, placed third in the jinshi examination of the twelfth year of Kangxi, was appointed compiler, and was transferred to Right Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 乞假歸。

translations.literal: He petitioned for leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned for leave to return home.

sentences.zh: 乾學卒，召補原官。

translations.literal: When Qianxue died, he was summoned to fill his former post.
translations.idiomatic: When Qianxue died, he was summoned to fill his former post.

sentences.zh: 累遷吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was successively promoted to Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was successively promoted to Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 命偕刑部侍郎綏色克如陝西，讞糧鹽道黃明受賄，擬罪失當，左遷詹事。

translations.literal: Ordered together with Vice Minister of Punishments Suiseke to go to Shaanxi to judge the case of Grain and Salt Commissioner Huang Ming accepting bribes, he proposed an inappropriate sentence and was demoted to Director of the Court of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered together with Vice Minister of Punishments Suiseke to go to Shaanxi to judge the case of Grain and Salt Commissioner Huang Ming accepting bribes, he proposed an inappropriate sentence and was demoted to Director of the Court of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 擢內閱學士，乞歸。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Bachelor of the Grand Secretariat, then petitioned to return home.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Bachelor of the Grand Secretariat, then petitioned to return home.

sentences.zh: 上南巡，賜御書「恭謹老成」榜額。

translations.literal: When the emperor toured the south, he bestowed an imperial inscription reading "Respectful, cautious, and seasoned in experience" as a plaque.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor toured the south, he bestowed an imperial inscription reading "Respectful, cautious, and seasoned in experience" as a plaque.

sentences.zh: 五十年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fiftieth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fiftieth year he died.

sentences.zh: 論曰：康熙初葉，主少國疑，滿、漢未協，四輔臣之專恣，三籓之變亂，台灣海寇之趒盪，措置偶乖，皆足以動搖國本。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: In the early years of Kangxi, the ruler was young and the state uncertain; Manchu and Han were not yet in harmony; the four regents were arbitrary; the Three Feudatories rebelled; Taiwan pirates surged and fell back; measures sometimes missed the mark—all enough to shake the foundations of the state.
translations.idiomatic: The appraisal says: In the early years of Kangxi, the ruler was young and the state uncertain; Manchu and Han were not yet in harmony; the four regents were arbitrary; the Three Feudatories rebelled; Taiwan pirates surged and fell back; measures sometimes missed the mark—all enough to shake the foundations of the state.

sentences.zh: 霨、廷銓、立德、溥當多事之日，百計匡襄；

translations.literal: Wei, Tingquan, Lide, and Pu, in days of many troubles, devised a hundred plans to support and remedy;
translations.idiomatic: Wei, Tingquan, Lide, and Pu, in days of many troubles, devised countless plans to support and remedy;

sentences.zh: 熙預顧命，參軍謀；

translations.literal: Xi received the dying emperor's charge and took part in military planning;
translations.idiomatic: Xi received the dying emperor's charge and took part in military planning;

sentences.zh: 正治等入閣，值事定後，從容密勿，隨事納忠；

translations.literal: Zhengzhi and others entered the Grand Secretariat when affairs had settled, calmly attending to confidential duties and offering loyal counsel as occasions arose;
translations.idiomatic: Zhengzhi and others entered the Grand Secretariat when affairs had settled, calmly attending to confidential duties and offering loyal counsel as occasions arose;

sentences.zh: 伊桑阿、阿蘭泰推誠佈公，受知尤深。

translations.literal: Yi Sang'a and Arantai were open-hearted and fair, and won especially deep imperial trust.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Sang'a and Arantai were open-hearted and fair, and won especially deep imperial trust.

sentences.zh: 康熙之政，視成、宣、文、景駕而上之，諸臣與有功焉。

translations.literal: The government of Kangxi ranks above the reigns of Cheng, Xuan, Wen, and Jing; these ministers all had a share in the achievement.
translations.idiomatic: The government of Kangxi ranks above the reigns of Cheng, Xuan, Wen, and Jing of the Han; these ministers all had a share in the achievement.
